news.Title: Onto Innovation vs. KLA: Which Semiconductor Stock is a Better Buy?
news.Content:
The semiconductor industry is booming, driven by AI, HPC, advanced packaging and increasingly sophisticated chip manufacturing processes. As chipmakers invest in next-generation production technologies, companies supplying semiconductor inspection, metrology and process-control equipment are well-positioned to benefit. Per a report from Fortune Business Insights, the global semiconductor metrology and inspection equipment market size is estimated to go from $16.26 billion in 2026 to $29.57 billion by 2034, at a CAGR of 7.8%.

Two notable players in this market are Onto Innovation, Inc . ONTO and KLA Corporation KLAC. Both companies provide technologies that help semiconductor manufacturers improve yields, maintain quality and manage increasingly complex manufacturing processes. However, their business models, market positions, growth opportunities and valuations differ.

For investors seeking exposure to semiconductor equipment stocks, the key question is which stock offers the better growth opportunity.

The Case for ONTO Stock

The company's growth opportunity is closely tied to three major trends. Increasing adoption of advanced packaging technologies, including 2.5D and 3D integration for AI accelerators, rising HBM demand, which drives additional inspection and metrology needs and the growing complexity of advanced semiconductor nodes, which requires more precise measurement and defect detection. Onto Innovation delivered record third-quarter revenue of $410 million, up 19% sequentially and 90% year over year. It raised its fourth-quarter revenue outlook to $430–$450 million, expecting more than 45% annual growth and strong visibility into 2027, with a backlog of over $1.3 billion.

Chip demand remains strong, driven by AI expansion, data center investments and sustained customer commitments. Advanced packaging remains a key growth driver, with Dragonfly platform revenue expected to increase more than 80% in 2026. Dragonfly G5 adoption is expanding across applications and customers, while rising demand for HBM, chiplets and 2.5D and 3D integration is increasing process control requirements. Revenue from advanced logic, DRAM and NAND nodes increased, with growth expected to exceed 35% in 2027. The Atlas G6 OCD platform is gaining traction, supporting tighter process control for increasingly complex semiconductor structures, including sub-2nm technologies.

Gross margin improved 60 basis points to 57.6%, with margins expected to exceed 58% in the fourth quarter. Continued operational efficiencies, supply chain localization and extended factory initiatives are expected to support further margin improvement into 2027. ONTO is well-positioned across CoWoS, EMIB and HBM packaging technologies as rising chip complexity increases inspection and metrology requirements. Power and silicon photonics revenue doubled in the third quarter, with further growth expected, while Dragonfly G5 front-end inspection applications could provide additional opportunities in 2027.

Story Continues

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, Onto Innovation faces tariff uncertainty, trade restrictions and rising memory, material, fuel and freight costs. Customer concentration remains high, with four customers contributing 57.1% of nine-month revenue. Taiwan and South Korea accounted for 58.9% of sales, exposing the company to regional disruptions and changes in customer spending. Rising inventory also increases the risk of buildup if orders are delayed.

Intense competition requires continued R&D investment, which rose to $45.1 million in the third quarter from $32.5 million a year earlier. Semilab USA also remains loss-making, recording a $2.8 million operating loss in the quarter. Onto Innovation recorded a $40.8 million unrealized loss on its Rigaku investment, widening the gap between GAAP EPS of 95 cents and non-GAAP EPS of $2.44. Quarterly valuation changes could add further earnings volatility.

The Case for KLAC Stock

With semiconductor manufacturers expanding production capabilities and adopting increasingly sophisticated manufacturing processes, demand for KLA's inspection and metrology solutions is likely to remain strong heading into calendar 2027. Its business benefits from several structural trends. These include AI infrastructure expansion, which drives demand for advanced process control; leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing, where smaller nodes increase the need for precise defect detection; increasingly complex DRAM and NAND technologies that require tighter manufacturing controls and growing adoption of advanced packaging, chiplet architectures and HBM, which create additional opportunities for inspection technologies.

KLA reported record fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, up 29% year over year, with gross margin of 62.7% and operating margin exceeding 46%. Management expects the wafer fabrication equipment market to exceed $200 billion in calendar 2027, with potential to surpass $220 billion by 2030. KLA expects to outperform industry growth through technology leadership, market share gains and increasing customer investments in leading-edge logic and DRAM.

Advanced packaging remains a major growth driver, with revenue expected to reach approximately $1.1 billion in 2027, up more than 70% year over year. Demand for higher-sensitivity inspection tools is increasing as packaging processes become more complex. Process control services revenue also grew 14%, supported by a larger installed base and demand for improved tool performance. KLA is expanding manufacturing capacity and strengthening supplier relationships to support growing demand. Improving component availability is easing some constraints, while additional investments in facilities, headcount and critical components aim to prevent supply bottlenecks.

Despite elevated memory costs, management expects to target a gross margin of 63-64% in 2027 through cost optimization and improved memory efficiency. Annual capital expenditures are expected to range from $600 million to $800 million, supporting capacity expansion and long-term growth. China revenue is expected to decline as a percentage of total sales, potentially reaching the low-20% range in 2027. Moreover, customer fab construction delays and infrastructure constraints could extend industry growth cycles into 2028. KLA remains focused on supply readiness, R&D investment and capturing opportunities across AI, advanced packaging and next-generation semiconductor nodes.

KLA continues to convert earnings into cash and return most free cash flow to shareholders. Free cash flow reached $1.34 billion in the fiscal first quarter. Capital returns included $936 million in buybacks and $305 million in dividends. KLA ended September 2026 with $4.74 billion of cash and marketable securities and $5.72 billion in carrying-value debt. Management targets returning more than 90% of free cash flow through 2030.

Share Performance Trajectory for ONTO & KLAC

In the past three months, ONTO stock has plunged 32.7% while KLAC has lost 22%.

Valuation Comparison

In terms of forward price/earnings, ONTO shares are trading at 16.81X compared with KLAC's 23.27X.

How the Zacks Consensus Estimate Compares for ONTO & KLAC

For KLAC, estimates have moved up for both fiscal 2027 and 2028 over the past 60 days as well.

Earnings estimates for ONTO have moved up for both 2026 and 2027 as well.

ONTO vs. KLAC: Which Stock is a Smarter Bet?

Both companies offer compelling exposure to the AI-driven semiconductor investment cycle, but KLA appears to be the more balanced investment opportunity. Onto Innovation's rapid growth is attractive, but investors must monitor whether its backlog converts into revenue and whether its improving margins remain sustainable. KLA's scale provides an important competitive advantage. Its substantial cash generation supports research and development, strategic investments, dividends and share repurchases.

KLAC currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), while ONTO has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). Consequently, in terms of Zacks Rank, KLAC seems to be the preferred choice. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Jim Cramer’s AI Hyperscale List: 5 Core Infrastructure Stocks for 2027
news.Content:
When a cloud company orders thousands of AI servers, the date it can put them to work often depends on when the local utility can deliver power. Contractors prepare the site and build the grid connection. Inside the facility, electrical equipment distributes power to the server racks, cooling systems carry heat away from the chips, and switches and fiber links allow processors across those racks to train a model together.

At the end of June 2026, CBRE tracked 7.48 gigawatts of wholesale data-center capacity under construction across eight major U.S. markets, with 80.4% already leased. For those projects, securing power on schedule can matter more than finding tenants. On October 28, California's grid operator approved a proposal that would let large customers connect before all transmission upgrades are complete if they can reduce their electricity use when the grid requires it.

For investors, the debate over how much power a data center can draw reaches beyond the utility. In August, CNBC's Mad Money host Jim Cramer explained why local opposition to new projects made him take a closer look at the order book of a company his Charitable Trust owned.

In November, a cloud operator raised its revenue forecast, lifting shares across the AI supply chain. A leading AI chipmaker ranked 10th in our ranking of the infrastructure stocks with the most upside implied by analysts' price targets following that report. However, the AI buildout extends well beyond chips, creating opportunities across the infrastructure needed to power, cool, and connect hyperscale data centers.

So, what are the core infrastructure stocks for 2027 in Jim Cramer's AI hyperscale list? We provided the expanded Jim Cramer's AI Hyperscale List: 10 Core Infrastructure Stocks for 2027 . The top 5 stocks are provided below.

Methodology

We reviewed his public comments from March through November 2026 and selected 5 stocks of companies that build, power, cool, or connect hyperscale AI facilities. We ranked the stocks in ascending order of market capitalization.

Jim Cramer's AI Hyperscale List: 5 Core Infrastructure Stocks for 2027

5. Equinix, Inc. (NASDAQ: EQIX )

Market Capitalization: ~$104 billion

Equinix, Inc. (NASDAQ:EQIX) gives cloud operators a way to expand without building every data center themselves. Through its xScale joint ventures, it develops and operates facilities where hyperscale customers lease capacity, measured in megawatts, to house and power their servers. In November 2025, when a shareholder asked whether to add to a position during Mad Money, Cramer explained what made him hesitant to put more money into Equinix . When another caller asked about Equinix on May 20, Cramer took a different view of the company's place in the data-center buildout .

Story Continues

Atlanta shows how much of Equinix's 2027 expansion customers have already committed to. The company expects two 60-megawatt xScale projects there to open in the second and fourth quarters, respectively. By the end of September, customers had leased all 120 megawatts. Across the xScale portfolio, 172 of the 186 megawatts under development were already leased. For investors, that shifts attention to the construction schedule. Each Atlanta project carries an estimated cost of $632 million, and customers are counting on Equinix to deliver the capacity on time.

4. Eaton Corporation plc (NYSE: ETN )

Market Capitalization: ~$137 billion

A data center can have its servers on order and still need equipment to distribute electricity to every rack. Eaton Corporation plc's (NYSE:ETN) electrical business is already seeing that demand in its results. Third-quarter data-center revenue rose approximately 65% year over year, while data-center orders over the trailing 12 months more than doubled. The figures cover different periods, but both point to customers committing money to electrical infrastructure. Management expects double-digit growth in the data-center and distributed IT market in 2027. Cramer singled out Eaton after the shares fell in May. During Mad Money's May 5 episode, he said:

Eaton for the electricity you need. By the way, that got hit, that was ridiculous. Just go buy that one. I'm not kidding… We own it for the Trust. It got hit ridiculously. We bought some today.

His October discussion of Eaton, along with a steelmaker, explained how the same construction project can generate orders for two very different industrial companies. For Eaton shareholders, the most telling figure in the next few quarters will be data center revenue as the company works through those orders.

3. GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE: GEV )

Market Capitalization: $212.5 billion

GE Vernova Inc.'s (NYSE:GEV) third-quarter results show how early customers are moving to secure gas turbines. The company had 64 gigawatts of gas power equipment under firm order and another 58 gigawatts of manufacturing slots reserved. One quarter earlier, the split was 53 gigawatts of firm orders and 63 gigawatts of reservations. The combined figure rose from 116 to 122 gigawatts, but the improvement in firm commitments was larger than that headline increase suggests. Management expected orders and reservations together to reach at least 130 gigawatts by year-end.

That demand extends well beyond 2027. GE Vernova plans to lift annual turbine production to 24 gigawatts in 2028 and 30 gigawatts in 2030. With near-term slots scarce, Cramer identified a decision on turbine pricing that could matter as much to shareholders as the next order. When shares fell after October earnings, he wrote on X, "I'm trying desperately to get into the brains of the GE Vernova sellers here but I don't know if they have any."

2. Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET )

Market Capitalization: ~$250 billion

Arista Networks, Inc.'s (NYSE:ANET) high-speed Ethernet switches connect the servers that do the work inside large AI clusters. The company expects its AI networking business to generate about $7 billion in 2027, roughly double its estimated 2026 level of $3.5 billion. It is targeting total revenue of about $18.5 billion in 2027, representing growth of 38% to 40%. The timing of major network deployments now matters to the growth rate of the entire company.

Arista entered that forecast period with third-quarter revenue of approximately $3.66 billion, up 58.5% and ahead of its $3.3 billion guidance. A September caller had asked Cramer what gave him confidence to keep buying Arista on declines after the shares had already climbed . Following the November 3 earnings call, Cramer commented

Those of us who still like tech, and I know a dwindling number, took heart that both AMD and Arista Networks reported very strong quarters after the session tonight… Jayshree Ullal, the CEO of Arista Networks, said terrific things about the data center networking on tonight's call.

1. Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO )

Market Capitalization: ~$377 billion

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) raised its fiscal 2027 forecast for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion, more than double the fiscal 2026 total. Management expects this business to account for 12% of total revenue, up from 6% a year earlier. Demand is also reaching customers outside the largest cloud companies. Cisco said fiscal first-quarter orders for Nexus data-center switches designated for AI deployments rose 47% year over year. In May, Cramer looked at whether Cisco's share price had already run ahead of its data-center opportunity . A subsequent pullback changed his view of the valuation, and during the November 6 episode of Mad Money, he said:

I have to tell you that this company reported back in May and the stock galloped from $102 to $130 in a matter of weeks thanks to great AI orders. But you live by the sword, you die by the sword. The stock has been caught up in the incredible tsunami of AI selling, and it's fallen all the way back to the $90s. Now, I think Cisco has gotten oversold. I think Chuck Robbins is going to deliver. I think this stock's actually cheap. I think it might be worth buying some if we can get through the CoreWeave-Nebius gauntlet. I'd not be a big buyer, but a small buyer.

The company's November 12 results gave him a chance to revisit the underlying business. After the report, he wrote on X, "Cerebras and Cisco beat. AI strong away from NVDA."

news.Title: Wall Street's Next Blockbuster Stock Split Arrives Later Today -- and This Industry Titan Has Skyrocketed Nearly 2,400% in Less Than 2 Years
news.Content:
Though the last four years have been dominated by the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) , AI isn't the only trend propelling the stock market to new heights. Stock-split euphoria has also played an important role -- and later today, Nov. 19, these two catalysts will converge.

After the close of trading today, Wall Street's next blockbuster stock split becomes effective , with memory and storage solutions specialist Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), which is up nearly 2,400% since its February 2025 debut, completing its first-ever split.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Investors commonly gravitate toward forward stock splits

A stock split allows a publicly traded company to alter its share price and outstanding share count by the same factor without affecting its market cap or underlying operating performance. Though there are two varieties of splits, investors tend to gravitate toward one and shy away from the other.

Reverse stock splits, designed to increase a company's share price, are often shunned by investors. This type of split is typically undertaken by struggling companies attempting to avoid delisting from a major stock exchange.

By comparison, investors tend to pile into companies announcing and completing forward stock splits. Forward splits make a company's stock more nominally affordable for everyday investors who can't purchase fractional shares through their broker.

More importantly, companies enacting forward splits are usually firing on all cylinders, with consistent sales and profit growth. If a public company needs to lower its share price to ensure retail investors can take part in its growth story, it must be doing something right.

After the close of trading today, Sandisk will effect an 8-for-1 forward split, reducing its share price to (presumably) a little over $100 and increasing its outstanding share count by a factor of eight.

Sandisk has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI data center build-out

Businesses are spending nothing short of an arm and a leg on the AI infrastructure build-out, and Sandisk has been one of the prime beneficiaries. The company's NAND flash memory solutions and solid-state drives are being gobbled up in bulk.

The AI data center expansion is benefiting Sandisk on both ends. The insatiable demand for its memory and storage solutions, coupled with ongoing supply shortages for AI hardware, has collectively beefed up its pricing power and lifted its gross margin to never-before-seen levels. Sandisk's gross margin reached 85% in the fiscal first quarter (ending Oct. 2) on $11.03 billion in sales.

Story Continues

Furthermore, at the company's mid-August Investor Day, CEO David Goeckeler outlined nearly $94 billion in signed contracts through fiscal 2030. Locking in future deals at premium price points can help Sandisk sustain its highest-ever gross margin.

But history might be Sandisk's biggest foe. Decades of history show that memory and storage solutions are highly cyclical. In other words, premium pricing power rarely lasts, with a contraction in price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples often indicating the late innings of a semiconductor cycle. Sandisk's forward P/E ratio of 3 offers all the hallmarks of an eventual bubble-bursting event in the AI arena.

news.Title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Micron Next?
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) may be the next tech stock to perform a stock split. Even after a lengthy correction, it still trades above $700 per share. It's normal for companies to initiate splits when they get closer to $1,000 per share, and investors already saw that unfold when fellow memory stock Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) announced an 8-for-1 split.

While an 8-for-1 split doesn't make sense for Micron at its current price, a smaller split may make sense in the near future.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Micron's fundamentals continue to improve

Micron's memory chips have become a vital part of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure , and investors have seen that truth play out in recent financial results. Each time that bears question the likelihood of Micron extending its gains, the company delivers robust earnings that beat expectations and hint at more future growth.

Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings capture how this story has been playing out. Micron told investors in the previous quarter to expect $50 billion in fiscal 2026 Q4 revenue at the midpoint, but it delivered $54.2 billion instead. Beating guidance helped Micron deliver 379% year-over-year revenue growth, and it told investors that fiscal 2027 will be even better.

If Micron continues to deliver tremendous fundamental growth, its stock could rally and reclaim its all-time high above $1,200 per share. A return to that level further justifies a stock split.

Strategic customer agreements offer multiyear revenue visibility

Micron has been securing multiyear deals with key tech companies, making it easier to forecast future revenue. These long-term deals were one of the biggest developments that shattered the bearish narrative about inventory gluts possibly weakening Micron's pricing power in the future.

This type of boom-and-bust cycle has been the norm in the semiconductor industry, but AI demand is still going parabolic. Grand View Research projects a 30.6% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) for the artificial intelligence industry through 2033. That suggests more demand for Micron's memory chips and additional pricing power.

The growth stock trades at a measly 4.5 forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, giving it a lower valuation than most bank stocks, which are achieving much lower growth rates. It's hard to find a stock that combines Micron's valuation and growth rates, and this one-two punch should ignite a stock rally in the months ahead.

Story Continues

Any rapid acceleration in Micron's stock price, similar to what investors saw earlier this year, would provide further justification for a stock split. Sandisk initiating its own stock split may prompt Micron to follow suit.

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be Sandisk’s Stock Price by the End of 2027
news.Content:
After an incredible rally in the first half of 2026, shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) have pulled back at an alarming pace in recent months.

The stock has retreated 60% since the beginning of July. Investors have been booking profits in Sandisk stock for various reasons. For instance, the broader semiconductor industry has been under pressure in recent months, as Wall Street is concerned about whether the incredible pace of spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is sustainable amid rising inflation, which has led the Federal Reserve to increase interest rates.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, this isn't the only reason why Sandisk stock has taken a beating. Concerns about the state of the NAND flash industry that Sandisk serves have played a central role in the stock's decline. Let's look at the factors impacting Sandisk stock lately and check if it can step on the gas in 2027.

Image source: Getty Images.

Potential NAND flash oversupply has pulled down Sandisk stock

Sandisk manufactures NAND flash storage products, including enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) that are used in AI data centers. The shortage of traditional hard-disk drives (HDDs) forced hyperscalers and AI companies to turn to SSDs to store huge data sets for training and inference workloads.

The demand for NAND flash storage significantly outpaced supply, creating a major shortage that led to a sharp price spike. Market research firm Gartner estimates that NAND flash prices will rise by 293% in 2026, as demand exceeds supply by 9%. The shortage is expected to persist into 2027, with demand exceeding supply by 5%. As a result, Gartner predicts a 30% increase in NAND flash prices next year.

This slower increase in prices has spooked investors, who now believe that Sandisk's days of hypergrowth could be coming to an end. Meanwhile, TrendForce reports that weak consumer demand for NAND has led to a 20% drop in spot prices in just two weeks. The shortage of data center graphics cards in China has led to a decline in enterprise SSD demand, thereby lowering prices.

These divergent views about the state of the NAND flash market in 2027 have weighed on Sandisk's shares recently. However, it is worth noting that lower spot prices don't necessarily mean that the NAND flash market will enter a downward spiral next year. That's because spot contracts usually involve small lot sizes and reportedly account for only 5% of NAND flash revenue.

Story Continues

Contract prices decide the market's direction, as NAND flash customers like to plan well in advance for their needs. This explains why Sandisk has already sold a large chunk of its NAND flash supply for the next two fiscal years under long-term agreements.

Sandisk management noted on the October earnings call that it has already sold 50% of its supply capacity for fiscal 2027 under long-term contracts. Even better, the company has demand commitments for two-thirds of its fiscal 2028 capacity. Management added that its long-term contract pipeline exceeds its supply capacity through the end of the decade.

So, Sandisk has demand visibility for the long run, which explains why its financial performance in fiscal 2027, which has just begun, is going to be solid.

A strong financial performance could send the stock higher in 2027

Sandisk's revenue in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended Oct. 2) increased by 378% year over year to $11 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share jumped from just $1.22 in the year-ago period to $49.51 in the previous quarter.

Importantly, analysts have become bullish on Sandisk's earnings growth prospects for the next three years.

SNDK EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Additionally, the recent pullback in this semiconductor stock has brought its price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio to just 7. The forward earnings multiple is even more attractive at 3.5. Sandisk is a screaming buy at these multiples, considering the impressive earnings growth it is poised to clock.

Assuming Sandisk's earnings jump to $289.05 in fiscal 2028 (which will end in June 2028) and it continues to trade at 7 times earnings, its stock price could reach $2,023 in a year and a half. That implies potential gains of 145%. Meanwhile, the stock has a 12-month median price target of $2,100, suggesting that Wall Street is even more bullish about its prospects over the coming year.

So, Sandisk can deliver significant upside by the end of 2027, which is why it would make sense to buy this AI stock following its recent decline before it steps on the gas once again.

news.Title: Dear Sandisk Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 20
news.Content:
Last month, SanDisk (SNDK) announced an 8-for-1 stock split that will take effect after the market closes on Nov. 19, with shares trading on a split-adjusted basis on Nov. 20. That means every share that SNDK stock investors hold will become eight shares, while the price will be divided by eight.

The company says the split is simply aimed at making shares more accessible, and that the overall market capitalization and ownership percentages will remain unchanged. So, the value of shares will stay the same.

More News from Barchart

Dear SpaceX Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 19

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for December 10

$1.6 Billion Loss: Billionaire Bill Ackman Says He Was 'A Little Bit Surprised' by Berkshire's $10 Billion Alphabet Bet, 'They Got It at a 6% Discount, But So What?'

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

A split won't suddenly make the business more valuable. However, there are other factors for investors to consider that may make SanDisk stock a potential buy. After all, easier access to shares may raise curiosity and excitement among investors, although that alone won't influence the company's true potential.

SanDisk's AI-Driven Rally Meets a NAND Pricing Reality Check

SanDisk stock has been on a meteoric run in 2026. Shares have gained roughly 227% year-to-date (YTD). This surge has arrived on the heels of soaring demand for NAND flash memory in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and a global chip shortage. In the company's latest quarter, revenue climbed 378% year-over-year (YOY) to $11.03 billion, driven by hyperscalers buying massive amounts of storage.

Recently, however, SNDK stock has cooled off from its highs, down 52% over the past three months. Analysts and investors are debating whether NAND prices can stay this high. If memory prices soften, SanDisk's pace of growth could be negatively impacted. Memory prices are dependent on the memory shortage, which could well be temporary.

Despite the enormous rally this year, SNDK stock looks significantly undervalued compared to its peers. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 3.5 times, which is cheaper than the sector average, while the P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 0.06 times times is also cheaper against the sector. That indicates that the stock trades at a deep discount relative to expected earnings growth.

That cheap multiple shows sky-high expected growth. Wall Street estimates that EPS could rise 226% year-over-year (YOY) in fiscal 2027. But there is still risk. If NAND prices start to slide, earnings could fall as well.

Story Continues

That said, the valuation looks relatively low for now, suggesting the market is pricing in further strong growth and some risk of moderation.

The 8-for-1 Split: What Changes and What Doesn't

There are a few important things every investor should know about the upcoming split. Shareholders who owned SNDK stock as of the Nov. 9 close will receive seven extra shares for each share held, issued after the market close on Nov. 19. Trading will begin in new share units on the morning of Nov. 20. Importantly, nothing about the value will change; 10 shares at a hypothetical $900 per share pre-split would become 80 shares at $112.50 per share after the split, still worth $9,000 total.

The market cap and ownership percentages will not change, either. The company's FAQ also notes that shareholders don't need to do anything to obtain the extra shares, as they will show up automatically. Even if you buy shares after the Nov. 9 record date but before Nov. 19, you will still get the additional shares, as the "rights" to the split stay with the stock until the ex-date.

Stock splits can lure new retail investors to the market just because the price appears smaller, while index funds will also re-balance around the split date. However, investors should remember that the split does not impact SanDisk's profitability or growth prospects. The core aim of SanDisk's business hasn't transformed.

SanDisk Reports Q1 Earnings

SanDisk's first-quarter fiscal 2027 results, reported on Oct. 29, came in above analysts' expectations. Revenue reached $11.03 billion, up 378% YOY, while net income climbed to $8.1 billion, or $52.60 per diluted share.

Data-center revenue surged 61% sequentially to $4.8 billion, driven by robust demand for enterprise storage linked to AI infrastructure, helping fuel both revenue growth and gross margins topping 85%. SanDisk also repurchased $5 billion worth of stock during Q1.

CEO David Goeckeler hailed the quarterly results, saying the company "started fiscal year 2027 with another quarter of strong performance, with robust and growing demand for our products driving outpaced growth in our data center business." In other words, SanDisk is riding a powerful AI-driven demand wave.

Looking ahead, management expects Q2 revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion as well as EPS of $55 to $57 on a pre-split basis. All told, SanDisk expects the party to continue for at least another quarter. Analysts do as well, although that hinges on prices remaining high.

What Are Analysts Saying About SNDK Stock?

Wall Street is generally bullish on SNDK stock. Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore remains positive on shares with an "Overweight" rating, recently raising his 2027 EPS forecast. Moore noted that NAND demand remains robust and that "the debate at this point is durability," saying that Morgan Stanley expects "pricing to remain strong as long as we remain at maximum AI investment."

Overall, SanDisk stock has a consensus "Strong Buy" rating based on 25 analysts with coverage. The average price target of $2,039.38 implies potential upside of around 163% from current levels.

news.Title: Dan Ives’ Top 10 AI Revolution Stock Picks: Inside The IVES ETF
news.Content:
Dan Ives, who now works at Yorkville Ives & Co., called the November 5 technology rout a "golden buying opportunity" in a note reported by CNBC on November 6. He wrote that the Democratic midterm win could move the peak in Big Tech capital spending growth to 2027 from 2028 or 2029, but that the AI buildout continues at a slower rate because it "does not cancel Christmas."

Ives still expects AI-linked capital spending of $3 trillion to $4 trillion over the next few years, and he said Big Tech companies are set to put more than $1 trillion into AI in 2027 alone. He said the sell-off treated tech stocks, and semiconductors especially, as though the midterm result would end the US buildout, which he argued it will not. He compared the sell-off to the ones during Covid and the tariff announcement, both of which he treated as chances to buy.

The Rout Behind Ives' Call

The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315.00 on November 5, closing more than 10% below its October 6 record and confirming a correction, Reuters reported. It was the index's deepest one-day drop in 19 months. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 12.2%, the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 3.44%, and roughly $3 trillion of market value disappeared. The VIX volatility gauge closed at 28.18.

Investors pointed to worries that Democratic gains would bring tighter AI regulation and slow data center construction. Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide, said the chip group is volatile and cyclical and that hedge funds had been selling it aggressively for weeks. The ETF behind this list is run by Wedbush Fund Advisers and tracks an index built from Ives' research, and readers looking at the stocks hit hardest can find more in our list of AI stocks that have sold off and still draw analyst interest .

Strategists Split on Whether the Worst Is Over

Stocks bounced on November 6. Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial, said, "AI has gone on trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict." Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services, said the selloff may prove to be a long-term buying opportunity. The Nasdaq still posted its fourth straight weekly decline.

On November 11, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq each rose more than 1%. Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt, described investor sentiment as swinging back and forth. For holders with a longer horizon, the companies building the data centers and chips behind AI are covered in our ranking of AI infrastructure stocks for the long term .

Story Continues

Our Methodology

For this article, we reviewed the holdings of the Wedbush Dan Ives AI Revolution ETF (IVES) and picked its top 10 stocks by portfolio weight, as of November 13, 2026. We ranked them in ascending order of portfolio weight, and we list each position's market value in the fund as of the same date. We also list each stock's number of hedge fund holders as of Q2 2026, from our database of 1,006 hedge funds.

At Insider Monkey, we are obsessed with what hedge funds do. The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

Dan Ives' Top 10 AI Revolution Stock Picks

10. IBM (NYSE:IBM)

Portfolio Weight: 3.96%

Market Value: $32.31 million

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 74

IBM reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 21. Software revenue grew 8%, and the Data business grew 19%. Bulls point to that pace as the reason to own the shares. IBM sells IT services, software and hardware to large organizations, and software is the part of that mix where customers are spending more.

Consulting is the weaker line. It brought in $5.3 billion, flat from a year earlier, and that holds total revenue growth to a modest rate. Infrastructure, the hardware unit, grew a little and filled part of the gap, so the company's growth did not rest on software alone. That leaves software as the one segment growing faster than the company as a whole.

Management also expects constant-currency revenue growth of 4 to 5% for the full year. IBM generated $7.8 billion of free cash flow in the first nine months and said the full-year figure should rise by more than $1 billion. We examined whether customer financing is flattering IBM's cash recovery in a separate piece, and the answer decides how much of the improvement carries into next year.

9. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD)

Portfolio Weight: 4.49%

Market Value: $36.66 million

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 164

Wedbush kept its Outperform rating and $600 price target on Advanced Micro Devices on November 4. The call came a day after AMD reported third-quarter 2026 results. AMD designs processors, graphics chips and AI accelerators for data centers, personal computers and gaming devices, and the data center is where its growth now comes from.

Data Center revenue, which includes Instinct accelerators and EPYC server processors, rose 97% to $8.5 billion in the third quarter. Data Center now makes up most of AMD's revenue. For the fourth quarter, AMD guided to revenue of about $17 billion. The company is ramping its Helios rack systems and MI450 accelerators with customers that include Anthropic, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, and that ramp is what supports the guide.

AMD shares fell 8.8% on November 13 in a broad chip selloff that day. Gaming is the soft spot, with revenue down 40% in the third quarter, so the company's growth depends on the data center continuing to expand. For what a premium valuation leaves AMD in room for error, see our analysis of its execution risk .

8. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)

Portfolio Weight: 4.52%

Market Value: $36.89 million

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 275

Wedbush cut its price target on Alphabet to $387 from $445 on October 29 and kept an Outperform rating. The cut came a day after Alphabet reported third-quarter 2026 results, in which Google Cloud revenue rose 103% to $30.7 billion. Alphabet also runs Google Search, YouTube and Android, and those businesses sit inside Google Services.

Total revenue grew 25%. Google Services grew, Search & other revenue grew, and operating income rose faster than revenue, which pushed the operating margin higher from a year earlier. The Gemini app reached 1 billion users in the period, which gives the company a large base to sell AI products to.

Wedbush kept the Outperform rating despite the lower target. The cut lowers the bar for the shares, even though cloud growth is running far ahead of the rest of the company. The unit's pace is the strongest argument bulls have, and the cut is the clearest signal of how much analysts are willing to pay for it. What Waymo could be worth inside Alphabet is a separate argument, and our piece on the company's valuation and Waymo takes it up.

7. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM)

Portfolio Weight: 4.65%

Market Value: $37.98 million

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 249

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 15. Net income rose 68.7% and grew faster than revenue did. The gross margin was 66.4%. Its U.S.-listed shares trade as American depositary receipts. TSMC is the contract chipmaker that builds processors designed by other companies, and chips made on its 2-nanometer process were 8% of wafer revenue. That share tracks how fast customers move to the process.

For the fourth quarter, TSMC guided to higher revenue than it reported in the third quarter and a gross margin of 65 to 67%. That range brackets the margin it just reported, so the company is telling investors that sales should keep climbing without a drop in profitability.

On November 4, Bernstein raised its price target on the company's U.S.-listed shares to $600 from $554 and kept its Outperform rating. The bull case rests on how fast the business is growing, and the bear case rests on price, since the stock already reflects a good deal of the AI buildout. Our analysis of TSMC's profit surge asks whether its next chip breakthrough can justify that valuation.

6. Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META)

Portfolio Weight: 4.70%

Market Value: $38.38 million

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 254

JPMorgan added Meta Platforms to its Analyst Focus List on November 9 and removed Alphabet, which leaves Amazon and Meta as the bank's preferred internet stocks. JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth kept an Overweight rating on Meta and wrote that "Meta's relative advertising strength is more evident than ever." He credited AI improvements in ad retrieval, ranking and targeting that raise advertiser conversions.

Meta runs the Family of Apps social platforms and the Reality Labs hardware unit. Revenue grew 26% to $64.60 billion in the third quarter of 2026, and operating income included a litigation charge. Capital spending reached $34.91 billion, which pushed free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion. Meta also gave a capital spending guide for 2026, so the cost of the AI buildout is the main pressure on its cash flow.

Anmuth also pointed to the company's Muse assistant, which has drawn 10 million sign-ups in the U.S. and Canada, and to the enterprise opportunity for its model API. WhatsApp's chances of becoming a large business beyond advertising get their own treatment in our analysis of Meta's messaging bet .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of META as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: STMicroelectronics Targets Double STM32 Revenue by 2028 as AI Demand Grows
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

STMicroelectronics aims to double STM32 revenue from 2025 to 2028 , with market share already back to about 23% and potentially reaching 25%–30% by 2028.

AI data centers are a major growth driver: ST expects microcontrollers to account for more than 30% of its data-center revenue in 2026 and data-center microcontroller revenue to double in 2027. Industrial automation, cooling and power delivery are also expected to support growth.

Further opportunities include automotive-grade STM32A chips, with revenue expected to start in 2028, and humanoid robotics, where a typical robot may use 100 or more microcontrollers. ST is also expanding its China supply strategy and adapting its software tools for AI coding agents.

STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen

STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM) aims to double revenue from its STM32 microcontroller business between 2025 and 2028, betting that demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure, industrial systems, robotics and automotive applications will expand its market.

Remi El-Ouazzane, president of the company's Microcontrollers, Digital ICs and RF Products Group, said during a conference call that STM32's market-share recovery was running about 12 months ahead of schedule. He said the business had returned to its nominal share of about 23% and could reach between 25% and 30% by 2028, with the result more likely to be toward the upper end of that range if the revenue goal is met.

→ The Next Nuclear Opportunity May Be in Fuel, Not Reactors: 3 Stocks to Watch

Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

El-Ouazzane said third-quarter 2026 revenue was 25% below its second-quarter 2023 peak, but the conditions behind those figures differed. The earlier peak benefited from inventory accumulation and price increases, he said, while distribution inventory is now below standard targets and the book-to-bill ratio has remained above one for four quarters.

Data centers and industrial markets

ST expects microcontrollers to account for more than 30% of its data-center-related revenue in 2026 and expects its data-center microcontroller revenue to double in 2027, El-Ouazzane said. The chips are used in optical connectivity, compute boards and power conversion systems.

→ Banking on AI: Can Upstart's New Bank Plan Turn Its Stock Around?

Industrial Chips Are in Rally Mode—5 Ways to Play

He said data centers would contribute a significant portion of STM32's growth but would not account for all of it. Industrial automation, cooling and power delivery are also growing, he said. The company expects a healthy industrial market through at least 2027 following an inventory correction during the prior three years.

Story Continues

ST has a strong position in microcontrollers used in optical transceivers, El-Ouazzane said, attributing it to the company's developer ecosystem and broad product portfolio. He said ST's planning assumes some loss of optical market share, given its current position.

Automotive and robotics opportunities

→ NVIDIA's Turbulence Could Have Ripple Effects Across Quantum Computing

ST is extending its STM32 platform into automotive-grade and higher-safety applications with the STM32A family. El-Ouazzane said revenue from the automotive products should begin in 2028, remain modest initially and become more meaningful in 2029.

Volkswagen has adopted STM32A, he said, citing the automaker as an example of demand for a unified platform and software ecosystem. El-Ouazzane added that ST's previously stated automotive microcontroller ambition remained valid, though it would take slightly longer than initially expected because of subdued market conditions.

In humanoid robotics, El-Ouazzane said a typical robot contains about 100 or more microcontrollers. He estimated that microcontrollers represent approximately 20% of the $800 in components per robot that ST could address. The company is working with leading industry participants, he said.

China, pricing and software

El-Ouazzane said ST is gaining STM32 market share in China through a strategy that offers the same product through two supply chains. The company delivered its first fully made-in-China STM32 products in the first quarter of 2026 and is extending the approach to additional product families.

He said the Chinese business was not dilutive to the group's gross margin, citing its product mix, and that market-share gains had not been driven by pricing. More broadly, ST intends to pass through cost increases without exploiting inflation, he said, adding that the company had potentially been overly aggressive with price increases in 2022 and 2023.

ST's STM32Cube software ecosystem is approaching 2 million active developers, El-Ouazzane said. The company is adapting its tools for AI coding agents and offers an AI-powered technical support assistant. It is also exploring possible bolt-on acquisitions that could strengthen its software ecosystem or its position in physical AI and humanoid robotics, he said.

About STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

STMicroelectronics is a global semiconductor company that designs, develops and manufactures chips and related products for customers in a range of industries. Its portfolio includes microcontrollers, analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits, power semiconductors, sensors, and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). The company's products are used in automotive systems, industrial equipment, communications devices, computers and consumer electronics. Its offerings support applications such as vehicle control and safety, factory automation, power management, and motion and environmental sensing.

news.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor Stock (TSM) Looks Too Cheap for Its Growth Outlook
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) stock looks too cheap for its growth outlook. The leading semiconductor foundry has fallen with the wider artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Shares are down roughly 26% since hitting an early-October peak of $487 , pulled down by a semiconductor sell-off triggered by leadership turmoil at Nvidia (NVDA) and fresh U.S. export curbs.

On the company's third-quarter earnings call in October, CEO C.C. Wei said, "demand for our leading-edge technologies continues to be extremely robust." The company's October 2026 revenue also grew 59.7% year-over-year.

While AI spending could disappoint, and China restrictions carry real consequences, TSMC's customers still need more advanced manufacturing capacity than it can supply. At about 15.38x next year's earnings, I think the sell-off offers an attractive entry point. I therefore rate TSM stock a Buy .

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

AI Fears Have Overshadowed TSMC's Position

AI fears have overshadowed TSMC's position, in my view. Investors are questioning whether hyperscalers will earn adequate returns on enormous infrastructure spending. Nvidia's leadership turmoil has intensified uncertainty around its China business. The announcement from Washington earlier this week adds tougher foundry-customer checks and restrictions targeting China's remote access to advanced AI computing .

Those developments can remove potential orders. Nvidia is a major customer, and a broader spending slowdown would affect TSMC. Its customer diversity doesn't protect it from an industry-wide retrenchment. Rather, it provides exposure across competing chip designs.

Nvidia could lose some accelerator share while AMD (AMD) gains it. Both companies rely on TSMC for advanced manufacturing. Google (GOOGL) and Amazon's (AMZN) custom accelerators provide other routes for AI spending to reach the foundry.

Broadcom's (AVGO) designs are another example. Its latest quarterly filing says TSMC produced roughly 95% of wafers supplied by its contract manufacturers during the first nine months. So changing winners among chip designers needn't mean fewer orders for TSMC. That distinction is central to my thesis. Customers can compete fiercely over AI profits while continuing to buy manufacturing services from the same supplier.

Story Continues

TSMC's process expertise makes switching difficult. Its enormous scale also helps spread development costs across a broad customer base. Building another leading-edge factory takes years, and matching its yields is a separate challenge. I think the market is applying too much of chip designers' uncertainty to the company that manufactures their products.

TSMC's October Revenue Strengthens the Growth Case

TSMC's October revenue strengthens the growth case after an already excellent Q3. Quarterly revenue rose 50.9% in Taiwan dollars , while net income increased 68.7%. Gross margin reached 66.4%, and 2nm contributed 8% of wafer revenue. Then last week's monthly report showed record October revenue of NT$586.9 billion (about $17.8 billion). That was up 14.7% sequentially and 59.7% year-over-year.

Revenue through October increased 43.3%. Growth accelerated after Q3, using the same local-currency comparison. That's difficult to reconcile with the idea that demand is already weakening materially.

Management's Q4 revenue guidance of $52.3 billion–$54.3 billion comes with 65%–67% gross margins. The steep 2nm ramp should help. More revealing, though, is the spending commitment beyond this quarter. TSMC expects $60 billion–$64 billion of capex in 2026, and management indicated that total investment over 2026–2028 should significantly exceed the previous three years.

Since leading-edge capacity takes years to bring online, customers plan capacity alongside TSMC well in advance. Management has even sent teams to check U.S. data center construction and power availability. Capex doesn't guarantee future sales, but collaborative capacity planning gives these investment figures far more weight than an optimistic forecast alone.

The 2nm family's annual capacity should more than double in 2027. A16 expands its high-performance computing offering, while A14 volume production is planned for 2028. Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate (CoWoS) packaging remains another scarce capability needed to assemble advanced AI systems. Agentic workloads are increasing demand for central processing units (CPUs), alongside inference accelerators and networking chips. Smartphones also support adoption of advanced processes.

Overseas expansion, including Arizona's next fab in 2027, adds capacity across more locations. So I see a manufacturing franchise expanding around several sources of demand, with customers already planning subsequent product generations.

TSMC's Valuation Leaves Room for Returns

TSMC's valuation leaves room for excellent returns if earnings follow current expectations. At today's price, consensus 2026 earnings per share (EPS) of $17.50 implies 20.55x earnings. The $23.39 estimate for 2027 reduces that to 15.38x. By 2028, $29.82 of EPS implies just 12.06x.

Those forecasts assume roughly 34% earnings growth next year and 27.5% afterward. This is an unusually modest price for this growth profile.

The opportunity has historical context. Forward P/E fell near 12x–13x in late 2022 and roughly 15x during parts of 2023. Patient buyers eventually benefited as earnings recovered and the shares rerated. I use that comparison cautiously.

Still, today's business is growing rapidly, with October revenue 59.7% higher. The technology position remains strong, and new capacity is being planned against customer demand. That makes a compressed multiple particularly interesting to me.

Customer concentration and Taiwan's geopolitical risks deserve a valuation discount. Export restrictions could tighten further, and enormous capex creates financial exposure if demand slows. Overseas fabs can also pressure margins. Eventually, leading-edge supply could catch up.

Still, even 16x the 2028 EPS estimate would imply roughly $477 per share before dividends. That illustrates why the return case can work without an extreme valuation. Further estimate increases would provide additional upside.

Is Taiwan Semiconductor Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Taiwan Semiconductor stock has a Strong Buy consensus on TipRanks, based on nine unanimous Buy ratings. The average price target of $563.75 implies roughly 57% upside from today's price levels. Wall Street therefore remains optimistic despite the recent deterioration in semiconductor sentiment.

Conclusion

TSMC will feel any genuine slowdown in AI investment. Yet its latest revenue figures show customers still demanding more leading-edge capacity. It can benefit as competing chip designers expand, even as market shares shift. At about 15.38x 2027 earnings, I think that position is attractively priced. October's revenue acceleration gives me more confidence in buying the decline.

news.Title: Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Is My Top Memory Stock for 2027.
news.Content:
Micron Technology and Sandisk have sizzled on the stock market in 2026. Both stocks have delivered impressive gains this year, despite witnessing a significant pullback in recent months amid the broader correction in tech stocks.

Micron stock , for instance, has gained 128% in 2026, as of this writing. Sandisk's gains are even bigger at 194%. Importantly, both memory companies can step on the gas once again in 2027, driven by the artificial intelligence (AI)-fueled demand for compute and storage.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

However, I think that Micron and Sandisk could be overshadowed by South Korean memory giant SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) next year. Let's look at the reasons why.

Image source: Getty Images.

SK Hynix's strong market share puts it in a solid position to capitalize on the memory market's growth

SK Hynix sells both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash memory. Counterpoint Research points out that the company controlled 29% of the DRAM market in the third quarter of 2026. It is second only to Samsung in this market. Micron, for comparison, has a 21% share of the DRAM market.

Meanwhile, SK Hynix's 19% share of NAND flash puts it ahead of both Micron and Sandisk, which have market shares of 15% and 11%, respectively. The South Korean company's healthy market shares in both DRAM and NAND flash explain why it reported phenomenal growth in Q3. SK Hynix's revenue surged 328% year over year to $79 billion, easily beating the consensus estimate.

The company's operating profit jumped 632% from the year-ago period and exceeded analysts' expectations. SK Hynix is well-placed to sustain such impressive growth. That's because the company has already sold more than half of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028 under long-term agreements with 14 customers.

Moreover, SK Hynix anticipates that memory demand will outstrip supply through 2030, indicating that the favorable environment fueling the company's stunning growth is sustainable. Also, SK Hynix is ramping up production of its next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, known as HBM4.

It points out that HBM4 has twice the bandwidth of the previous-generation HBM3E chips and 40% higher power efficiency. SK Hynix notes that HBM4 revenue and shipments will surpass those of HBM3E in the current quarter, which should bode well for the company's margins. That's because HBM4 reportedly carries a 24% premium per gigabyte (GB) over the previous generation, HBM3E.

Story Continues

What's more, SK Hynix controls a third of the global HBM market, higher than Micron's 18% share. This is another reason to buy SK Hynix, considering that the global HBM market's revenue could surge to a whopping $641 billion in 2030, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. The firm has significantly upgraded this guidance from its earlier estimate of $260 billion, noting that the average price of HBM will more than double over the next four years.

So, there is a strong likelihood that SK Hynix's revenue growth will outpace Wall Street's expectations.

Here's why SK Hynix is clearly a better bet than Sandisk and Micron

SK Hynix's lead over Micron and Sandisk in DRAM and NAND flash should ideally give it greater pricing power over its rivals. This probably explains why analysts expect SK Hynix's earnings per share to increase at a much faster pace in the long run.

Also, SK Hynix's valuation is in line with Micron and Sandisk's multiples.

MU PE Ratio data by YCharts

So, even though SK Hynix stock hasn't made a bright start on the U.S. stock market following its listing on the Nasdaq this year, it remains worth buying on account of its red-hot growth, cheap valuation, and the ability to outperform Micron and Sandisk. In the end, I won't be surprised to see this AI stock's fortunes turn around in the New Year, and buying it while it trades at cheap multiples seems prudent.

news.Title: NVIDIA's Leadership Woes: Buy TSMC & ASML Despite Supply-Chain Risks?
news.Content:
NVIDIA 's NVDA leadership crisis has created significant uncertainty in the semiconductor space, raising questions about manufacturing commitments, AI infrastructure investments and the future direction of the company. The board's decision yesterday not to reinstate co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO has added another layer of uncertainty for suppliers and investors.

The uncertainty has also unsettled investor sentiment across NVIDIA's supply chain, weighing on the stock performance of key partners Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, popularly known as TSMC, and ASML Holding ASML. Month to date, TSMC and ASML have declined 9.5% and 10.8%, respectively, reflecting broader concerns surrounding NVIDIA's leadership transition and its potential implications for semiconductor demand.

November Stock Performances So Far: NVDA, TSM & ASML

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, NVIDIA's latest quarterly results suggest that its underlying business momentum remains strong. The company reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.47. Revenues of $115.84 billion surpassed expectations by 7.07% and more than doubled year over year.

Nevertheless, strong financial performance does not entirely eliminate concerns about the company's leadership transition and its potential implications for future supplier relationships. During its earnings call, NVIDIA confirmed that its board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation, appointed longtime CFO Colette Kress as Interim CEO and initiated a search for a permanent successor.

Against this backdrop, TSMC and ASML are great investment choices. While both companies face indirect or direct exposure to potential changes in NVIDIA's manufacturing requirements, their broader AI-related growth opportunities and strong operating fundamentals provide reasons for optimism. Both stocks currently carry a positive Zacks Rank, making them worth buying amid the semiconductor industry's evolving risks and opportunities.

NVIDIA's Supply-Chain Risks: How Much Should Investors Worry?

NVIDIA's leadership transition could affect supplier relationships and future manufacturing commitments if a successor adopts a more cautious approach to capacity reservations and capital allocation. Reuters reported on Nov. 12 that Asian suppliers were preparing for potential changes in NVIDIA's expansion plans, with one Taiwanese supplier expressing concern that a new CEO might be less aggressive in securing manufacturing capacity.

Story Continues

However, NVIDIA's Nov. 17 earnings offered some reassurance. Apart from better-than-expected numbers, Data Center revenues jumped 110% to $107.6 billion. NVIDIA also projected fourth-quarter revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, sending its shares higher in after-hours trading following the earnings announcement.

Interim CEO Kress said the company remained engaged with suppliers, including TSMC. NVIDIA also reported $390 billion in purchase commitments in the third quarter, reflecting confidence in long-term infrastructure demand.

Why TSMC Is a Buy Now

TSMC's position as the world's leading advanced-chip foundry makes it a key beneficiary of AI accelerator demand. Its third-quarter 2026 revenues increased 41.2% year over year, while earnings per ADR surged 57.5% to $4.60. Gross margin reached 66.4%.

High-performance computing (HPC) accounted for 68% of third-quarter revenues, up from 57% a year earlier, while smartphones contributed 21%. However, NVIDIA's importance to TSMC cannot be overlooked. J.P. Morgan estimates that NVIDIA accounts for approximately 22% of TSMC's 2026 revenues, exposing the foundry to potential changes in the chipmaker's manufacturing requirements and capacity commitments.

Image Source: JP Morgan

Nevertheless, strong demand from other major customers provides some diversification. TSMC described AI demand as extremely robust and maintained its 2026 capital expenditure outlook of $60-$64 billion. It expects fourth-quarter revenues of $52.3-$54.3 billion and a gross margin of 65-67%. Its advanced-node leadership and expanding capacity support its long-term growth prospects despite NVIDIA-related uncertainty.

This Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock is expected to report 2026 earnings growth of 63% on revenue growth of 40.9%.

ASML Remains a Buy Too

ASML, a leading supplier of advanced lithography systems, is well-positioned to benefit from rising semiconductor manufacturing requirements driven by AI. Its third-quarter 2026 net sales reached €11.7 billion, while gross margin was 57.5% and net income totaled €5 billion.

ASML has no direct dependence on NVIDIA's chip orders. Its exposure is indirect through equipment demand from foundries and memory manufacturers investing in advanced production capacity. This broader customer exposure provides some insulation from NVIDIA-specific uncertainties.

The company recently noted strengthening customer demand and warned that planned equipment supply for 2027 and 2028 might not fully meet customer requirements. ASML expects 2026 revenues of €44-$45 billion, with EUV system sales projected to grow more than 45%. Strong order momentum, technological leadership in EUV lithography and expanding customer capacity requirements support its long-term growth prospects.

This Zacks Rank #2 stock is expected to report 2026 earnings growth of 66.4% on revenue growth of 33.9%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: NVIDIA vs. Cisco: One AI Stock Looks Like a Better Buy Now
news.Content:
Despite NVIDIA Corporation 's NVDA strong quarterly performance, leadership uncertainty and rising artificial intelligence (AI) spending concerns could pose a challenge in the future. However, Cisco Systems, Inc .'s CSCO stable management and diversified business portfolio could position it as a better stock to buy now. Let's explore –

NVIDIA Sees Record Growth, Issues Strong Q4 Revenue Guidance

NVIDIA delivered another strong quarter, with revenues surging 103% year over year to $115.8 billion in the fiscal third quarter of 2027, according to the company's Nov. 17 press release. It also posted a 20% sequential rise from $96.2 billion in the previous quarter. NVIDIA's triple-digit growth rate highlighted that strong AI spending benefited the company, with tech companies investing significantly in computing capacity.

The Data Center business remains its primary growth driver, with revenues jumping 110% year over year and 21% sequentially to $107.6 billion. This result shows NVIDIA is making the most of hyperscalers' massive investments in AI-driven data centers. By the way, NVIDIA is converting its impressive revenue growth into noteworthy profits as well. Its GAAP net income jumped 105% year over year to $65.3 billion.

Looking ahead, NVIDIA expects revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%, in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2027, which would represent a 12% sequential rise. That's a strong revenue growth projection, especially since it doesn't include China-related Data Center compute revenues. NVIDIA also expects its earnings outlook to remain strong in the fiscal fourth quarter.

NVIDIA Is Dominating AI, But Is Cisco the Better Investment?

NVIDIA's strong fiscal third-quarter performance and optimistic fiscal fourth-quarter outlook suggest the company is not only benefiting from the AI boom but also converting that growth into solid revenues and earnings growth. However, the latest controversy surrounding NVIDIA's boardroom drama and the subsequent ouster of Jensen Huang as CEO is a significant concern for investors in the future.

NVIDIA will lose a visionary leader, whose continuous innovation helped the company maintain a competitive position in the rapidly evolving AI market. His earlier investments in graphics processing units helped NVIDIA establish a competitive advantage against its peers. He also played a crucial role in building partnerships among major tech players, and his departure could give an undue advantage to rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. AMD.

Story Continues

Moving ahead, NVIDIA's capability to sustain an extraordinary growth rate without Huang at the helm will be closely monitored, and any leadership uncertainty could dent investors' confidence. But as NVIDIA grapples with leadership succession, Cisco stands out for its stable succession planning and management continuity. The company's CEO, Chuck Robbins, has held the position since 2015 and has assured investors that in his absence, the company's strategic decisions and execution won't be hampered.

Growing concerns about the sustainability of AI spending could create additional uncertainty around NVIDIA's future growth trajectory. Cisco, on the other hand, has a diversified revenue stream, making it less dependent on the AI boom. It can benefit from broader IT spending, providing additional growth opportunities, and could offer greater resilience if AI-related spending moderates.

Cisco reported record revenues of $18.5 billion in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, up 24% year over year, according to the company's Nov. 12 press release. However, Cisco's revenue growth wasn't only dependent on AI investments by hyperscalers; it was broad-based, across various business segments like networking, cybersecurity, collaboration and software.

Additionally, similar to NVIDIA, Cisco is translating its revenue growth into stronger earnings and demonstrating operational efficiency. Its GAAP net income jumped 59% year over year to $4.6 billion in the fiscal first quarter. Furthermore, management has raised its full-year 2027 revenue guidance to $74.8-$75.8 billion and increased its earnings expectations, reflecting confidence in future business growth.

Therefore, while NVIDIA offers greater AI-driven growth potential, Cisco's management stability, diversified revenue streams, and positive outlook make it an attractive investment for investors looking for more balanced growth. Cisco currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), while NVIDIA has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Dan Ives sends a strong signal ahead of the Anthropic IPO
news.Content:
Wall Street's biggest AI test of the year is days away. Anthropic is set to go public this week, and Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives called the deal an "important step" for the AI buildout, noting that it marks "the first time a U.S. frontier lab carries a standalone public market price, uncluttered by an ad business or a rocket business."

The numbers are enormous. Anthropic and some existing shareholders plan to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, raising up to $64.4 billion, with trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT set to begin November 19. A separate $26 billion private placement could lift the total raise to about $90.4 billion.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, according to the Anthropic prospectus.

The cornerstone group is led by Google, Nvidia and AMD, with Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC also taking part. At the top of the range, the offering implies a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

Why Ives calls the Anthropic IPO an important step

For Ives, the most telling detail is who is buying. "The cornerstone book is the tell," he wrote, explaining that the seven anchors are Anthropic's chip suppliers, cloud hosts, and distribution partners.

That means hyperscaler spending and Anthropic's contracted demand "are the same dollars viewed from both ends," according to Seeking Alpha.

Also read: Jim Cramer has a new warning for investors watching Anthropic

Some of those commitments are large. Nvidia and Google have each committed $10 billion to the private placement, while AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC partners are contributing $6 billion in total.

Those ties cut both ways. "For the hyperscalers, Anthropic is at once a customer, competitor, sales channel and investment," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney said after the company's first filing, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

An $895 billion demand signal for chips and clouds

Ives sees Anthropic's spending plans as a gift to the AI supply chain. With Google, Amazon and Microsoft all serving as backers, customers and compute suppliers, the company's $895 billion in compute commitments give the Street a "multi-year demand signal for chipmakers and the clouds that host them" that it "can now underwrite from a public filing rather than infer from capex guides," according to Seeking Alpha.

The filing spells out how big that bill is. About $70 billion comes due within a year and nearly $450 billion by the end of 2030, roughly seven times the cash and short-term investments Anthropic held at the end of September. Broadcom, Google, SpaceX's AI unit, and Amazon hold the largest commitments.

Story Continues

The total has grown fast. Anthropic's confidential filing earlier this year pointed to at least $518 billion in infrastructure spending over the next decade with six partners, and about 80% of that was non-cancelable or had to be paid regardless of actual usage, according to TheStreet.

Anthropic's own leaders acknowledge the risk. "With the way you buy these data centers, if you're off by a couple years, that can be ruinous," CEO Dario Amodei has said, while the filing notes that much of its revenue "is not subject to long-term contractual commitments."

Demand looks strong, much like SpaceX

Investors appear eager anyway. The IPO is reportedly about six times oversubscribed, even as fears of overspending and soaring debt have pushed investors away from tech stocks in recent weeks.

The Nasdaq posted its biggest monthly loss in over a year in October. Goldman Sachs, one of the lead banks, forecasts revenue above $685 billion by 2030, according to Bloomberg.

The book filled quickly. Orders reached about twice the shares on offer by the first day of the roadshow and six times by the end of the fourth, faster than SpaceX's pace. Still, some investors questioned whether Anthropic can hold its lead as Google and others catch up, and one said the company had not provided detailed answers to some of the questions raised.

Ives expects a "successful transaction" like SpaceX's, but that deal also serves as a reminder that a hot debut is no guarantee. SpaceX priced at $135 and opened at $150 on June 12, hit a record $225.64 four days later, yet was trading near $143 by mid-November, according to Seeking Alpha.

Valuation skeptics are lining up as well

"If they go public at 1.33 trillion dollars and grow to 4 trillion, that's only 200% upside," said University of Florida professor Jay Ritter, known as "Mr. IPO," who noted that Nvidia's 1999 IPO valued it at only about $350 million. New Constructs went further, calling it "the most ridiculous IPO of 2026" and valuing Anthropic at roughly $150 billion, as reported by TheStreet.

More Artificial Intelligence:

AI investments fail when companies ignore the hard part of transformation

Morgan Stanley issues a fresh warning about AI stocks

CrowdStrike gives companies a 'kill switch' as bots go off script

Not everyone is as upbeat about the setup either. "They will be profitable probably in the next quarter or two. But then they're going to start going back into losses," said Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg, who called it "a pretty challenging setup for their IPO."

Buyers will also inherit unusual risk disclosures. The prospectus devotes about 93 pages to risk factors and warns that advanced AI systems could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity."

OpenAI could be the next in line

Ives believes a strong debut would clear the way for OpenAI, which is raising privately at a reported $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of an expected 2027 listing. "A 1.25 to 1.4 trillion (or higher) Anthropic that prices and trades well in the months ahead validates the capex that every name in the AI supply chain is being underwritten on," he said.

The timeline matters. OpenAI has told investors it plans to list in 2027, and a stumble by Anthropic could push that window back. A strong close, on the other hand, would provide the entire frontier AI sector with a public-market benchmark for the first time.

Whether Ives's "important step" turns into a lasting win will depend on how the stock trades after this week's pricing.
