news.Title: Cisco Drops 7% Post Earnings: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems CSCO shares have dropped 6.7% in the past three trading sessions after the company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Nov. 12. Shares fell 6.2% in the Nov. 13 trading session, despite CSCO reporting record revenues and earnings and raising its fiscal 2027 guidance. The primary concerns were declining gross margins, higher component costs, slowing product-order growth and uncertainty surrounding the sustainability of AI-driven demand. However, does the dip offer an opportunity to take a position in CSCO shares? Let's find out.

Cisco Suffers From Margin Pressure, Moderating Order Growth

Investor concerns around margin pressure and the quality of forward growth despite very strong top-line results have been plaguing Cisco shares. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, non-GAAP gross margin contracted 250 basis points (bps) year over year to 65.6%, while non-GAAP product gross margin declined 350 bps to 63.7%. The contraction primarily reflected a higher mix of hardware revenues, particularly AI networking infrastructure and elevated memory costs. Cisco's growing exposure to relatively lower-margin hardware raised concerns regarding its ability to sustain profitability as AI infrastructure revenues accelerate.

Cisco increased its fiscal 2027 hyperscaler AI infrastructure revenue forecast to $9 billion from $7.5 billion. However, the rapid expansion of this hardware-intensive business is expected to weigh on product margins. Moreover, moderating product order growth is a concern. Although total product orders increased 21% year over year in the reported quarter, growth slowed from 35% in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. This raised concerns that Cisco's near-term demand momentum might be moderating following a period of significant expansion. The company faces tougher year-over-year comparisons, particularly in campus networking, and is also expected to suffer from uneven spending patterns of hyperscale customers.

Cisco now expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, implying a sequential decline from the reported $18.52 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected between $1.34 and $1.36, below the fiscal first quarter's reported figure of $1.40 per share. Although the company raised its fiscal 2027 outlook, the sequential moderation in revenue and earnings raised concerns regarding the near-term growth trajectory.

Year to date (YTD), Cisco shares have returned 23.5%, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's appreciation of 3.5%. Cisco has underperformed peers, including Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE and Arista Networks ANET, but outperformed Broadcom AVGO over the same time frame. Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Arista Networks have appreciated 91.9% and 42.3% YTD, respectively, while Broadcom has dropped 1.3%.

Story Continues

CSCO's Price Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Strong AI Infrastructure Demand Aids Cisco's Prospects

Cisco is benefiting from accelerating investments in AI infrastructure as hyperscalers expand their data center networking capabilities. The company secured three new AI infrastructure design wins in the fiscal first quarter, bringing the total to 18 over the past five quarters. CSCO's Silicon One P200, G200 and G300 networking platforms, alongside Acacia coherent optics, are strengthening the company's competitive position in high-bandwidth AI connectivity. The growing design-win pipeline provides additional revenue opportunities extending into fiscal 2028 and beyond.

Cisco is witnessing stronger demand for AI networking infrastructure from enterprises, neocloud providers and sovereign cloud operators. First-quarter orders for Nexus data center switches associated with AI deployments increased 47% year over year. The company's collaboration with NVIDIA and Supermicro to expand Secure AI Factory offerings is strengthening CSCO's ability to deliver integrated AI infrastructure. The deployment of AMD GPU-based infrastructure using Cisco Silicon One systems for HUMAIN in Saudi Arabia highlights opportunities in sovereign AI projects. Increasing adoption of hybrid and private AI infrastructure should provide incremental growth opportunities.

Cisco's expanding campus networking portfolio also represents a significant growth opportunity. First-quarter campus networking orders increased 14% year over year, supported by growing adoption of next-generation switching, routing and wireless products. Wireless orders increased more than 20%, while Wi-Fi 7 accounted for more than 60% of access-point orders. With next-generation products representing less than 10% of campus switching orders, Cisco has substantial room for further adoption. The company estimates a network refresh opportunity exceeding $100 billion, supported by enterprise modernization and increasing bandwidth requirements.

Fiscal 2027 Earnings Estimate Revisions Positive for CSCO

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is currently pegged at $5.21 per share, up by a nickel over the past 30 days, indicating year-over-year growth of 20.3%. Fiscal 2027 revenues are pegged at $74.60 billion, indicating 17.8% growth over fiscal 2026's reported figure.

Cisco Systems, Inc. Price and Consensus

Cisco Systems, Inc. price-consensus-chart | Cisco Systems, Inc. Quote

The consensus mark for CSCO's second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings is currently pegged at $1.25 per share, up by a penny over the past 30 days, indicating year-over-year growth of 20.2%. Quarterly revenues are pegged at $18.13 billion, indicating 18.1% year-over-year growth.

CSCO Shares Are Trading at a Premium

Cisco shares are trading at a premium, as suggested by the Value Score of D.

In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, CSCO is trading at a premium of 5.05X, higher than the broader sector's 4.79X and Hewlett Packard Enterprise's 1.11X.

However, Cisco shares are trading at a discount compared with Arista Networks and Broadcom. In terms of the forward 12-month P/S, Arista Networks and Broadcom shares are trading at 13.19X and 9.09X, respectively.

CSCO Stock's Valuation

Conclusion

Cisco's recent share-price decline offers an attractive entry point for long-term investors, supported by strong AI infrastructure demand, expanding hyperscaler relationships and a multi-year campus networking refresh cycle. Growing adoption of Silicon One, Acacia optics and integrated AI networking solutions, alongside positive earnings estimate revisions, strengthens its growth prospects. Although margin pressure, elevated component costs and premium valuation remain concerns, Cisco's expanding AI opportunities and improving earnings outlook justify a bullish stance on CSCO shares.

CSCO currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Does Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock go any direction but down? For the past five trading sessions in a row, it's been one loss after another for Sandisk shareholders -- and Wall Street isn't helping.

As StreetInsider.com reports, Zacks Research pulled a complete 180 on Sandisk this morning, downgrading the memory chipmaker from "strong buy" to "hold." (Zacks' own website, however, states that it actually downgraded Sandisk stock to hold two days ago and set its price target at $1,881.)

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Whichever report is correct, the effect on Sandisk stock is obvious: As of 11:30 a.m. ET, Sandisk stock is down another 4.4%.

Image source: Getty Images.

What's ailing Sandisk

Downgrade or no downgrade, the story on Sandisk seems unchanged today. Investors are punishing Sandisk -- and other AI stocks -- on worries that AI chip sales will slow in the wake of Nvidia's CEO scandal . As one of the world's biggest manufacturers of NAND flash memory chips, this would be bad news for Sandisk.

These worries were exacerbated -- and seemingly confirmed -- yesterday when semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis reported that it sees capital spending on AI chips in 2027 falling 19% below previous estimates, 2028 spending 28% below expectations, and 2029 spending 41 % below estimates.

What's next for Sandisk

All that being said, here's some good news that may be getting lost in the shuffle: Zacks' downgrade to "hold" flies in the face of Zacks' price target of $1,881 per Sandisk share. With Sandisk stock priced below $762 today, this implies that Zacks expects the stock to shoot up nearly 150% over the next year!

Call me a contrarian, but that sounds more like a "buy" than a "hold" rating to me.

news.Title: Forget Nvidia: 5 Stocks Wall Street is Betting on Right Now
news.Content:
Stocks ended a jumpy week with gains on paper and a sour finish. Reuters reported on November 13 that the S&P 500 fell 0.40% and the Nasdaq fell 0.91% on the day, yet the S&P 500 still rose 2.51% for the week, ending four straight weekly declines. The rebound did not survive the final session, and the reason sat in the bond market rather than in earnings.

Hot Inflation Forces a Rethink on Rates

Consumer price data released on November 10 showed headline inflation rising 0.4% in October, above forecasts, with the core measure also coming in hotter than expected. Two-year Treasury yields jumped about 19 basis points that day, the biggest one-day move since April 2025, as traders abandoned hopes of a pause.

Policymakers have since leaned toward tightening. One Federal Reserve governor has argued for a December increase, possibly of half a point, and a regional Fed president wants at least two more increases of 25 basis points from a policy rate of 3.75% to 4.00%. Yahoo Finance reported that the 10-year yield stayed above 5% after leaping more than 13 basis points on November 12, and that traders now treat a December hike as a certainty.

The pressure has reached households. Freddie Mac put the average 30-year mortgage rate at 7.11% for the week ended November 12. Investors asking which beaten-down names might still be worth owning can browse 10 Oversold AI Stocks: Where Wall Street Analysts Are Spotting 50%+ Upside .

Chip Stocks Take the Brunt

Semiconductors absorbed the worst of it. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 3.4% on November 13, and technology was the weakest of the 11 S&P 500 sectors with a 1.7% decline. The VIX volatility gauge moved back above 20. A separate Yahoo Finance staff report said chip stocks had shed more than $650 billion in two days as the 10-year yield climbed about 30 basis points in a week to roughly 5.15%, its biggest weekly rise since April 2025.

Other data pointed the same way. The dollar reached a 19-month high, and Reuters reported that October producer prices were up 6.5% from a year earlier, while the two-year yield finished the week near 4.87%, its largest weekly increase in more than two years.

For anyone who wants a longer view of the sector, 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade looks past the current swings. The Fed meets on December 9, and the inflation and jobs reports that arrive before then are likely to move stocks more than any single earnings release.

We shared the expanded list of Forget Nvidia: 10 Stocks Wall Street is Betting on Right Now here. You can find the top 5 stocks below.

5. Sea Limited (NYSE:SE)

Market Cap: $41.40 billion

Average Upside Potential: 77.1%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 86

Jefferies cut its price target on Sea Limited (NYSE:SE) to $142 on November 10 and kept a Buy rating. The firm lowered its estimates for the gaming business and cited macro uncertainty in online shopping, along with AI spending that is weighing on its EBITDA estimates.

Sea reported its third quarter of 2026 the same day. Revenue was $8.6 billion, but adjusted earnings of $0.78 per share missed the $0.99 analysts expected. Net income rose 34% from a year earlier, so the miss was about expectations rather than a decline in profit. Management kept its full-year targets and announced a new share buyback. Sea runs the Shopee marketplace, the Monee financial services arm and the Garena games business.

Monee is where bulls and bears disagree most. Revenue there grew quickly, but credit-loss provisions rose 82.3%, and Bank of America Securities cut its price target the next day over a margin miss in the unit and a jump in capital spending. Bulls call the loan book a growth engine. Bears want proof that losses stay in check. We covered the stock's earlier rally in Sea Limited (SE) Jumped 15%, But Can the Rally Last? .

4. Celestica (NYSE:CLS)

Market Cap: $30.31 billion

Average Upside Potential: 86.5%

Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 63

Celestica (NYSE:CLS) said on October 26 that it expects about $40 billion of revenue in 2027, nearly double the $21.0 billion it projects for 2026.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenue was $5.83 billion and adjusted earnings were $3.30 per share. The company raised its 2026 outlook and guided fourth-quarter revenue above the third-quarter level. UBS analysts raised their price target to $453 on October 28 and kept a Buy rating. Celestica builds networking and computing hardware for cloud providers, so investors read its order book as a sign of data center spending.

Customer concentration is the main risk. Its ten largest customers made up 85% of revenue, according to its quarterly filing, so a pause in orders from one or two of them would show up quickly. Number of Hedge Fund Holders: 131

Summit Insights cut Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX) to Hold from Buy on October 28, the day after the company reported its fiscal first quarter of 2027, and gave no price target.

The report itself was strong. Revenue was $4.2 billion, non-GAAP gross margin was 57.8%, and non-GAAP earnings were $7.68 per share. Free cash flow was $1.5 billion, and the company paid down $1.2 billion of its debt. CEO Dave Mosley said the company is in a multi-year growth phase and pointed to its HAMR drive technology. Seagate makes hard drives and storage products for data centers. It also raised its quarterly dividend.

Bulls say most of its high-capacity drive supply for data centers is already allocated through 2028, which gives them visibility on demand. Summit Insights' downgrade is about valuation rather than demand. The debate is how much of a peak in hard drive profits the shares already reflect. Bears say record results are hard to repeat once supply and pricing stop improving. We looked at what investors expect from the stock in Can Seagate's (STX) AI-Driven Growth Justify Its Sky-High Expectations? .

BTIG analyst Andrew Harte reiterated a Buy rating and a $250 price target on October 30. The company sells fixed-income instruments that give investors exposure to bitcoin and uses the money to buy more of it. Bulls like the plan to keep selling those instruments to fund purchases, which makes the stock a leveraged way to own bitcoin. Because results swing with the price of bitcoin, a result like this one can reverse.

Bears focus on what the company owes. Preferred dividends were $419.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, and common shareholders sit behind a large stack of preferred stock. The company's own bitcoin yield measure is negative for the year, and a profit that comes from the asset's price says little about the business. Goldman Sachs cut its price target on Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) to $2,000 from $2,200 on October 30 and kept a Buy rating, citing very limited additions to NAND supply and a better product mix.

Revenue in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 was $11.0 billion, up 23% sequentially. The company guided fiscal second-quarter revenue to $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective November 19. CEO David Goeckeler pointed to durable free cash flow. Sandisk makes NAND flash storage devices.

Bears say gross margin gains have stalled since the report, so the question is whether memory profits have peaked. If supply stays tight, margins should hold. If it does not, the earnings that look so large in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 could shrink quickly. The split does not change the value of the company, but it lowers the price per share. Bulls say the stock still trades at a low multiple of expected earnings, which leaves room for it to hold up even if growth slows. news.Title: Can Arista Strengthen AI Networking With Its New Etherlink Offerings?
news.Content:
Arista Networks, Inc. ANET is expanding its artificial intelligence (AI) networking portfolio with new Etherlink R4 platforms designed to enable secure, low-latency AI inferencing across geographically dispersed data centers. The solutions aim to meet growing demand for reliable network connectivity as agentic AI and complex inferencing workloads require faster data processing closer to end users.

The latest platforms are built on advanced 5nm silicon and powered by Arista Extensible Operating System. They deliver up to 60% lower power consumption than alternative solutions based on 7nm and 16nm chips. They also integrate high-performance routing, encryption, multi-tenancy, workload steering and deep packet buffering to ensure reliable network performance across distributed AI environments.

The company's new Etherlink lineup includes the 7020HR4 and 7020R4 routing platforms for secure compute and storage connections. The 7282R4 improves network reliability with dual Supervisor Engines, while the 7280R4 supports high-speed optical connections at 400 Gbps and 800 Gbps with integrated encryption. Arista also introduced a 25.6 Tbps pluggable optical line system with C-band amplification, optical multiplexing and an optical time-domain reflectometer for in-service network testing and validation.

The 7020HR4 is expected to be available in early 2027, while the remaining products are available now. The launch strengthens Arista's position in AI networking by combining energy-efficient routing, secure connectivity and high-capacity optical solutions, while helping customers improve AI inferencing performance, meet data sovereignty and regulatory requirements and reduce infrastructure operating costs.

How Are Competitors Advancing in AI Networking?

Arista faces competition from Cisco Systems, Inc. CSCO and NVIDIA Corporation NVDA. Cisco is strengthening its AI networking capabilities with advanced optical technologies designed to support higher bandwidth and more efficient data transmission across AI data centers. Its Silicon One P200 technology connects geographically dispersed AI data centers, enabling faster and more reliable data movement. Cisco is expanding its switching portfolio with the new 51.2 Tbps Silicon One G302, designed to improve connectivity and performance in high-density AI data center networks.

NVIDIA is expanding its AI networking business with Spectrum-X Ethernet switches and Quantum-X InfiniBand platforms designed for large-scale AI computing. These technologies help improve communication between AI processors and reduce network congestion during complex workloads. NVIDIA is advancing its optical interconnect solutions to increase network bandwidth, improve power efficiency and support growing AI infrastructure demands.

news.Title: Here's Why KLA (KLAC) Is a Great 'Buy the Bottom' Stock Now
news.Content:
A downtrend has been apparent in KLA (KLAC) lately. While the stock has lost 5.5% over the past week, it could witness a trend reversal as a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session. This could mean that the bulls have been able to counteract the bears to help the stock find support.

The formation of a hammer pattern is considered a technical indication of nearing a bottom with likely subsiding of selling pressure. But this is not the only factor that makes a bullish case for the stock. On the fundamental side, strong agreement among Wall Street analysts in raising earnings estimates for this maker of equipment for manufacturing semiconductors enhances its prospects of a trend reversal.

What is a Hammer Chart and How to Trade It?

This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'

In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.

When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.

Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.

Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.

Here's What Increases the Odds of a Turnaround for KLAC

There has been an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions for KLAC lately, which can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

Story Continues

Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 5.4%. What it means is that the sell-side analysts covering KLAC are majorly in agreement that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

If this is not enough, you should note that KLAC currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Moreover, a Zacks Rank of 2 for KLA is a more conclusive indication of a potential trend reversal, as the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator that helps investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve.

news.Title: NVIDIA Q3 Earnings Beat on Data Center Demand & Rubin Ramp-Up
news.Content:
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA posted third-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $2.68 per share, up 111% year over year. Earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.50 by 7.20%, reflecting strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and a rapid Vera Rubin rollout.

Revenues surged 103% year over year to $115.84 billion, topping the consensus mark of $108.19 billion by 7.07%. Data Center sales drove top-line growth.

NVDA's Data Center Momentum Accelerates

Data Center revenues surged 110% year over year and 21% sequentially to $107.61 billion. Vera Rubin generated nearly $20 billion in its first quarter of production shipments, marking NVIDIA's fastest product ramp. Continued demand for Blackwell Ultra also supported growth.

Hyperscale revenues reached $60.14 billion, rising 71% year over year and 23% sequentially. AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise revenues soared 195% year over year and 18% sequentially to $47.47 billion, benefiting from Rubin shipments to neoclouds and frontier labs building their own facilities.

NVIDIA Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NVIDIA Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NVIDIA Corporation Quote

NVIDIA's Edge Computing Sales Extend Gains

Edge Computing revenues were $8.23 billion, up 42% year over year and 14% sequentially. Higher sales of Blackwell workstations and computing systems for physical AI applications supported the increase, although elevated memory and system prices continued to pressure consumer PC demand.

Within reportable segments, Compute & Networking revenues totaled $106.0 billion, soaring 108% year over year and 20% sequentially. Graphics revenues surged 62% year over year and 25% sequentially to $9.8 billion, reflecting broader demand across NVIDIA's computing platforms.

NVDA's Margins Benefit From Product Mix

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 140 basis points year over year to 74.9%, helped by a richer Blackwell Ultra product mix. The metric contracted 10 basis points sequentially as the company began ramping Rubin infrastructure.

Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 52% year over year and 7% sequentially to $8.84 billion, reflecting higher compute infrastructure and employee compensation costs. Despite this increase, non-GAAP operating income surged 116% year over year to $77.88 billion, supported by robust revenue growth.

NVIDIA's Cash Generation Funds Expansion

Cash flow from operating activities reached $48.25 billion compared with $23.75 billion a year earlier and $24.08 billion in the previous quarter. Free cash flow was $43.78 billion compared with $22.09 billion in the year-ago period. The company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.

Story Continues

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities totaled $53.51 billion at quarter-end. Inventories increased to $39.72 billion from $31.58 billion sequentially to support Rubin production. Accounts receivable reached $81.03 billion, while days sales outstanding increased to 64 from 60, reflecting shipment timing and extended payment terms for certain customers.

NVDA's AI Commitments Expand With Demand

Supply and capacity commitments increased to $390 billion from $279 billion in the second quarter, primarily due to multiyear memory procurement. Cloud service and data center lease commitments totaled $102 billion, reflecting investments to support product development and the company's infrastructure needs.

Additional neocloud commitments totaled $32 billion, contingent on partners securing financing and deploying systems. Maximum gross exposure under guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support tied to an Ohio data center campus. Management said it had made no payments on these guarantees.

NVIDIA Raises Its Fiscal 2028 Growth View

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects revenues of $130 billion, plus or minus 3%. The outlook includes an additional week and assumes no Data Center compute revenues from China. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are projected at 71-72%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $10.7 billion, while GAAP expenses are projected at $11 billion. Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to approximately 75% from 70%, citing stronger demand and additional supply capacity. It anticipates gross margins of 72-73% in fiscal 2028.

NVDA's Zacks Rank & Stocks to Consider

NVIDIA currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks worth considering in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN, Applied Materials AMAT and KLA Corporation KLAC. TXN currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), while AMAT and KLAC carry a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) each. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Texas Instruments' 2026 earnings has moved northward by 41 cents to $8.99 per share over the past 30 days and calls for a year-over-year jump of about 65%. TXN shares have soared 70.6% year to date (YTD).

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Applied Materials' fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $18.62 per share, up by 34 cents over the past 30 days, indicating a year-over-year rise of 44.5%. AMAT shares jumped 35.9% YTD.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for KLA's fiscal 2027 earnings has been revised upward by 29 cents to $5.73 per share over the past 30 days, suggesting a year-over-year increase of 52.4%. KLAC shares have rallied 19% YTD.

news.Title: 證交所：創意、欣興、金像電、華通違約交割　合計2.66億
news.Content:
（中央社記者曾仁凱台北2026年11月18日電）台灣證券交易所今天公告，包括創意 (3443) 、欣興 (3037) 、金像電 (2368) 、華通 (2313) 等4家上市公司，出現鉅額違約交割，合計違約金額達新台幣2.66億元。其中華通和欣興為今年第2度發生鉅額違約交割。

證交所公告，中信託忠、玉山景美等2家證券商通報，創意發生鉅額違約交割，總金額9453萬元。

國泰敦南、國泰敦二、華南淡水、元大莒光、永豐天母、凱基松山、永豐板盛、群益鳳山、第一彰化、國泰館前、元大松山、富邦經紀、永豐金、元大雙和、元大永寧等15家證券商通報，欣興發生鉅額違約交割，總金額約5204萬元。

證交所表示，永豐敦南、永豐板盛、永豐金、國泰敦南、元大松山、國泰館前、國泰敦三、華南頭份等8家證券商通報，金像電發生鉅額違約交割，總金額約2616萬元。

華南台南、兆豐松德、國泰館前、群益海山、國泰敦二等5家證券商通報，華通發生鉅額違約交割，總金額約9360萬元。

根據台股「T+2」交割制度，證交所今天公告違約交割，為本週一（11月16日）的股市交易違約。當天台股開低走低，終場重跌2635.04點，創台股史上第2大收盤跌點。

連同今天公告的4起鉅額違約交割，今年上市公司鉅額違約交割案累積達19起。在此之前，包括旺宏 (2337) 、佳必琪 (6197) 、新日興 (3376) 、欣興、華通、國巨 (2327) 、友達 (2409) 、禾伸堂 (3026) 、南亞科 (2408) 、聯茂 (6213) 、致茂 (2360) 、台郡 (6269) 和景碩 (3189) 都曾發生鉅額違約交割，其中包含國巨3次，欣興、華通各2次。

news.Title: Stock Market Correction: 2 AI Stocks With 130% and 160% Upside, According to Wall Street.
news.Content:
The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) entered correction territory earlier this month amid concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom. But history says the sell-off is a buying opportunity. In the last decade, the index returned an average of 21% during the year following its first close in correction territory.

Wall Street analysts see substantial upside in the following AI stocks:

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) trades 57% below its high. But Wall Street's median target price of $2,100 per share implies 160% upside from its current share price of $809.

CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) trades 46% below its high. But Wall Street's median target price of $115 per share implies 130% upside from its current share price of $50.

Here's what investors should know.

Image source: Getty Images.

Sandisk: 160% upside implied by Wall Street's median target price

Sandisk manufactures storage devices based on NAND flash memory. Historically, the company has focused on consumer products such as SD cards, USB flash drives, and portable solid-state drives (SSDs). But Sandisk is increasingly targeting the enterprise SSD market to capitalize on growing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Sandisk is smaller than competitors Samsung and SK Hynix , but its joint venture with Japanese manufacturer Kioxia offers supply chain security and cost advantages. The companies share investments in semiconductor fabrication equipment, allowing Sandisk to purchase NAND flash memory wafers at cost plus a small markup rather than pay market prices.

"NAND flash is emerging as the only economically viable solution to deliver the capacity, performance, and efficiency required to keep models accessible for real-time inference at scale," said CEO David Goeckeler. "This shift in understanding the critical nature of our technology comes at a time when our product differentiation is strongest."

Sandisk reported strong financial results in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended in October. Revenue rose 378% to $11 billion, driven primarily by quadruple-digit sales growth in the data center segment. Sandisk also reported triple-digit sales growth in the edge segment, which supplies flash storage for industrial equipment and consumer devices like laptops and gaming consoles.

Story Continues

However, Sandisk is currently reaping the benefits of a memory chip supply shortage fueled by intense demand for AI infrastructure. NAND prices are projected to quadruple this year due to that shortage. But the memory industry is highly cyclical. A supply glut could develop by 2029 as manufacturers expand production capacity, driving prices (and profits) lower.

Sandisk trades at 6.5 times earnings. That seems cheap for a company whose earnings are forecast to grow at 40% annually over the next three years. But earnings could drop sharply during the next industry downturn, and uncertainty concerning the timing and severity of that downturn make Sandisk a risky bet.

CoreWeave: 130% upside implied by Wall Street's median target price

CoreWeave operates a cloud computing platform purpose-built for artificial intelligence. While general-purpose clouds like Amazon and Microsoft support a broad range of tasks, CoreWeave rents access to large clusters of powerful GPUs that are primarily used for a single purpose: training and running AI models.

CoreWeave's competitive edge comes from its specialized infrastructure and expertise in managing large GPU clusters. The company routinely achieves leading results at the MLPerf benchmarks, objective tests that evaluate AI systems across training and inference tasks. In September, independent research company SemiAnalysis recognized CoreWeave as the best AI cloud for the third consecutive time.

"CoreWeave continues to set the benchmark for AI cloud performance by demonstrating strong technical execution and operational maturity in managing large-scale AI solutions," wrote Dylan Patel, chief analyst at SemiAnalysis.

CoreWeave reported solid third-quarter financial results, sending shares 25% higher the next day. Revenue rose 168% to $3.6 billion, up from 112% in the prior quarter. Contracted revenue backlog soared 138% to $132 billion. But debt-fueled expansion is still a concern. Interest expense consumed 23% of revenue, and non-GAAP loss widened to $529 million.

CoreWeave trades at 2.7 times sales. That looks cheap when Wall Street expects revenue to increase at 96% annually through 2028. That means CoreWeave currently trades at 0.6 times projected 2028 sales. Of course, the company must still prove its debt-fueled growth can generate sustainable profits, and rising interest rates will make profitability harder to reach. But the stock could deliver substantial upside if CoreWeave executes.

news.Title: 群聯參展SC26 秀三大新世代儲存技術
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-18 16:35:05 新聞中心 發佈

NAND控制晶片暨AI運算儲存解決方案領導廠群聯電子(8299)今(18)日於SC26超級電腦大會(Supercomputing 2026)展示三項新世代儲存技術創新，涵蓋 PCIe Gen6、運算式儲存(Computational Storage)及混合式儲存架構(Mixed Media)。群聯執行長潘健成表示，下一個世代的資料儲存與AI(人工智慧)運算競爭，不會只由CPU或GPU效能決定，更重要的是能否有效率地傳輸、處理及儲存，以支撐 AI 發展所需的龐大資料；讓儲存不再是系統效能的瓶頸，而是驅動 AI 與高效能運算算(High-Performance Computing，HPC)創新的重要關鍵。

群聯電18日於SC26超級電腦大會(Supercomputing 2026)展示三項新世代儲存技術創新，涵蓋 PCIe Gen6、運算式儲存及混合式儲存架構。群聯表示，隨著AI與HPC工作負載持續攀升，傳統運算與儲存基礎架構正面臨效能瓶頸。群聯透過全新技術突破，提升資料傳輸速度、將運算能力延伸至儲存端，並進一步最佳化NAND儲存裝置的效能與容量運用，為新世代運算需求提供更完整的儲存解決方案。

群聯表示，本次展示有三大技術亮點：

一、PCIe Gen6：突破資料傳輸速度瓶頸

隨著 AI 工作負載需要處理及傳輸規模日益龐大的資料，PCIe Gen5 的頻寬逐漸接近極限。新一代 PCIe Gen6 將每通道傳輸速率提升一倍，達到 64 GT/s，為大幅提升儲存效能開啟新的可能性；然而，更高的傳輸速度也對訊號完整性帶來更嚴峻的挑戰。

二、Computational Storage(運算式儲存)：讓運算更靠近資料所在位置

傳統儲存架構必須在 SSD、記憶體及 CPU 之間大量搬移資料，容易形成頻寬瓶頸，即使持續提升處理器效能，也難以單獨解決這項問題。群聯的運算式儲存技術重新設計傳統運算流程，將資料處理能力直接整合至儲存裝置內，讓運算能在資料所在位置完成，減少不必要的資料搬移。

三、Mixed Media(混合式儲存架構)：兼顧高效能與大容量，不再二選一

傳統企業級儲存系統通常需要分別配置高效能快取 SSD 與大容量 SSD，迫使企業在速度、耐用度及儲存容量之間取捨，同時也占用寶貴的伺服器SSD槽位。群聯混合式儲存架構突破傳統設計，將兩種不同特性的 NAND 儲存媒體整合於單一 SSD 中。

群聯執行長潘健成表示：「下一個世代的資料儲存與AI運算競爭，不會只由CPU或GPU效能決定，更重要的是能否有效率地傳輸、處理及儲存，以支撐 AI 發展所需的龐大資料。群聯持續挑戰傳統儲存架構的限制，透過頻寬倍增、將智慧運算能力直接帶到資料所在位置，以及突破效能與容量之間長期存在的取捨，推動儲存技術持續創新。這些技術展現了群聯對未來運算的願景：讓儲存不再是系統效能的瓶頸，而是驅動 AI 與高效能運算創新的重要關鍵。」

慧榮拓AI儲存，SC26展出Gen6控制晶片

群聯Gen 6企業級SSD送樣，AI業務占比升至65%

news.Title: 才剛填息！輝達概念股華邦電突翻臉 重挫逾4%
news.Content:
輝達供應鏈的記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）今（18）日除息交易，每股配息2元，參考價108.5元，早盤一度衝上115元順利填息，但受亞洲科技股走弱與新台幣續貶拖累，盤中翻黑下探104.5元、跌幅逾4%。分析師表示，儘管短線賣壓沉重，基本面依舊亮眼。但現在正在跌、籌碼還很亂，千萬別急著現在衝進去接刀。

華邦電今日進行除息交易，每股配發現金股利2元，除息參考價為108.5元；若以昨日收盤價110.5元計算，現金殖利率約1.81%。

華邦電今日股價開高走低，早盤一度衝高至115元、順利完成填息，但受亞洲科技股走弱及新台幣續貶拖累，盤中由紅翻黑，最低下探104.5元，跌幅逾4%。

倫元投顧分析師王春盛指出，儘管市場對記憶體景氣仍抱持期待，但受大盤氛圍與匯率貶值影響，短線賣壓沉重。回歸基本面，華邦電第三季營收達823.31億元，季增37.6%，毛利率高達70.6%，單季EPS為7.58元，累計前三季EPS達15.32元，獲利表現亮眼。操作策略上，王春盛建議持股者可先觀察除息後股價能否止穩並重啟填息走勢；空手者則不宜急於追價，宜等待量縮止穩、外資買盤回籠後再分批布局，並嚴設停損。

華邦電日前召開法說會，總經理陳沛銘指出，市場普遍預期2027年記憶體缺貨狀況恐比今年更嚴重，且下半年緊縮力道將強於上半年。

陳沛銘指出，當前產業景氣呈現嚴重的「AI強、非AI弱」分化現象，第四季消費性需求已出現修正，甚至有客戶直言PC做三季累了，「第四季要休息」，但預期公司第四季營運雖能保持成長，但增長力道將不如前幾季強勁。

news.Content:
Investing.com-- Shares of chipmakers and cloud computing firms rose sharply in premarket trading on Wednesday after blowout quarterly earnings from sector giant Nvidia helped restore faith in the artificial intelligence trade.

By 04:10 ET (09:10 GMT), Nvidia rose 2.9%, while rival AMD rose 2.6%. Intel added 1.6%, Arm jumped 3.4%, Broadcom rose 2.1%, and Super Micro added 4.2%. Marvell, Micron, and U.S.-listed shares of SK Hynix gained more than 3% each.

Among cloud computing stocks, Oracle added 2.5%, while neoclouds Coreweave and Nebius added 5.9% and 7.8%, respectively.

European semiconductor stocks followed suit, rallying after the market open on Wednesday. Siltronic surged nearly 8%, Technoprobe rose 4.3%, while BE Semiconductor, ASML, ASM International, Aixtron and Soitec rose around 3% each. Infineon and STMicroelectronics gained about 2%.

Nvidia posted stronger-than-expected earnings for its third fiscal quarter, and flagged continued, growing demand for its advanced processors from the AI industry.

The print came amid troubled times for the chipmaker, which recently ousted CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.

Huang's exit fueled concerns over more regulatory scrutiny towards Nvidia, while investors also questioned whether new management would continue the chipmaker's massive investments in some of its largest cloud customers, which made it a de-facto central bank for AI infrastructure financing.

But Tuesday's strong earnings helped reinforce the notion that Nvidia's core business remained solid despite the governance scandal. CFO and now interim CEO Colette Kress also reiterated that the company will continue to invest in some of its customers, albeit with more "discipline" in how it commits capital going forward.

Kress said AI-fueled demand for Nvidia's chips remained robust and was likely to stay strong in the coming quarters. She forecast stronger-than-expected revenue in the current quarter, and said gross margins were set to improve in the coming year.

Story Continues

JPMorgan called the results a "positive datapoint" but said they were not a "clearing event" for concerns about the data center market.

Separately, Citi analysts said the print "reinforced our core investment thesis that demand remains very strong, supply constraints are easing, and interim management is confident enough to raise long-term growth expectations."

Nvidia and broader tech stocks were nursing deep losses heading into Tuesday's print, amid growing uncertainty over what Huang's ouster may imply for the broader AI trade.

Nvidia had slumped nearly 25% so far in November, while the SOX was nursing a near 10% decline.

While Tuesday's print helped spur some buying, Nvidia still traded well below record highs hit earlier in 2026.

The stock still faces overhangs, with U.S. lawmakers increasingly scrutinizing the firm over potential chip sales to Chinese entities.

Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter have agreed to testify before Congress on the matter.

But separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission had opened a probe into Nvidia.

news.Title: ‘How Could You Not?’ Says Investor About Sandisk Stock
news.Content:
Sandisk ( NASDAQ:SNDK ) is selling flash memory to AI data centers about as fast as it can make it, but that has done little for investors' morale recently. The stock keeps falling anyway, with shares drifting lower since their late-June peak.

The past couple of weeks have made things worse. AI stocks dropped after the Democrats' midterm sweep raised fears that tighter rules could slow data center construction, and then fell again when Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO on Nov. 12. Monday was the third losing day in a row, and traders are now waiting for Nvidia's quarterly report after the bell today.

The stock currently sits about 65% below its June record. That's just days before Sandisk's 8-for-1 stock split takes effect on Nov. 20.

Promotion

BLACK FRIDAY SALE

Get 75% Off TipRanks Premium and unlock powerful investing tools to make smarter, more confident investment decisions

Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter , and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Learn more about TipRanks Premium

The problem, says investor Infinity Curve (IC), has less to do with the company and more to do with the market still treating Sandisk like the old boom-and-bust memory maker and missing how much the business has changed. In fiscal Q1 2027, revenue jumped 378% year over year to $11 billion, and non-GAAP gross margin came in at 85.1%. Management expects $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion in revenue this quarter.

IC accepts that margins like that won't last forever. Still, management said about 60% of the sequential sales jump came from higher volume rather than higher prices. The investor sees that as a sign of real demand. Data centers drive most of it. That segment's revenue rose 61% from the prior quarter to $4.8 billion, and exabytes shipped grew about 330% YoY.

IC argues that AI inference needs more storage than DRAM or HBM can supply at a sensible cost. Larger context windows and more complex agentic tools are two reasons. IC gives little weight to Sandisk's high-bandwidth flash plans and bases the thesis on products already on the market.

The investor's biggest reason for optimism is the contract book. Sandisk has $88.9 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPOs), mostly from multiyear supply deals that cover about half of fiscal 2027 bits and two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits. About 95% of those customers are investment grade, and many have put up collateral. IC is careful here. The deals don't fix margins and only partly protect Sandisk, so the cycle hasn't gone away. Even so, keeping a bit more profit in a downturn could justify a much higher valuation.

Story Continues

The cash keeps coming in, too. Sandisk generated about $5.7 billion of adjusted free cash flow last quarter. IC's only complaint is that $5 billion of it went to buybacks at today's prices, and the investor would have liked to see more kept back for a rainy day. A roughly 40% jump in receivables from the prior quarter is also on IC's radar, though as something to keep an eye on rather than a red flag.

At about 6.5x trailing earnings, the stock already looks cheap, but IC doesn't lean on that number, since it could reflect peak profits. Even if gross margin falls to 72% on $42 billion of yearly revenue, which would still be very high for a memory maker, IC finds the shares have plenty of room to run.

None of this means the NAND cycle has gone away. NAND prices could fall if Samsung, SK hynix or Micron ramp up production, and that would hit the sales not covered by contracts. Outside data centers, things are already softer, with consumer revenue down 29% from the prior quarter. Sandisk also relies on its Kioxia venture for almost all of its wafers, and on a fairly small group of large customers.

Still, IC believes the contracts should help Sandisk hold on to more of its earnings when the next downturn comes.

Bottom line, Infinity Curve rates SNDK a Strong Buy. (To watch Infinity Curve's track record, click here )

So does the analyst consensus, a rating based on 11 Buys and 3 Holds. At $2,131, the average price target implies shares will gain 163% over the coming months. ( See SNDK stock forecast )

news.Title: 4 Dates That Could Move the Stock Market in Epic Fashion This Week. Here's What Investors Need to Know.
news.Content:
Wall Street is heading into one of the most consequential trading weeks of 2026, with several major events capable of influencing investor sentiment converging at once. Between Nov. 17 and Nov. 20, investors will receive Nvidia 's (NASDAQ:NVDA) fiscal third-quarter earnings report, the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes, and the initial public offering (IPO) of artificial intelligence (AI) developer Anthropic. Meanwhile, memory manufacturer Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) is preparing to execute an 8-for-1 stock split that could attract attention from retail investors.

These events arrive during a particularly uncertain period for the stock market. Concerns around AI valuations, interest rate policy, political uncertainty, and corporate leadership shakeups have introduced unusual levels of volatility into an otherwise multiyear bull market.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's take a look at five important events taking place this week and what investors should be watching.

Image source: Getty Images.

Nov. 17: Nvidia's earnings will be about more than financials

Nvidia is scheduled to report earnings after the market closes on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The company guided for revenue of $108 billion, representing roughly 89% growth year over year.

Ordinarily, investors would be focusing on whether Nvidia exceeds this forecast and provides encouraging guidance for the upcoming quarter. However, this earnings announcement comes under much different circumstances following Jensen Huang's unexpected resignation as CEO. As a result, another quarter of robust financial growth will likely take a back seat to questions surrounding Nvidia's leadership transition.

Huang played an instrumental role in transforming Nvidia into the dominant supplier of AI accelerators, making his departure a meaningful source of uncertainty for investors. During the earnings call, my hunch is that analysts will be trying to get some clarity around the company's succession plans and its ability to maintain competitive advantages without its former leader.

Nov. 18 and 19: Anthropic's IPO and the Federal Reserve collide

Anthropic is expected to finalize the pricing of its IPO on Nov. 18. The start-up behind the Claude chatbot is indicating an offering price in the range of $70 to $78, potentially raising around $64 billion at the upper end. Such a debut would rank among the largest IPOs in stock market history , making it an important test of demand for AI investments.

Story Continues

Anthropic is subsequently expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Thursday, Nov. 19. The offering could generate widespread enthusiasm throughout the AI ecosystem, particularly among companies with financial and commercial relationships with the developer. Amazon , Alphabet , and Space Exploration Technologies are among the companies investors could scrutinize as Anthropic's valuation and infrastructure spending commitments receive greater attention.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve is scheduled to release minutes from its October monetary policy meeting at 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 18. Smart investors will look for clues about whether the Fed is considering another interest rate hike before the end of the year. Any indication that interest rates could remain elevated might pressure growth stocks, whose valuations are highly sensitive to changes in borrowing costs.

Nov. 20: Sandisk's stock split could be another catalyst for AI stocks

The week's final major event involves Sandisk, which is preparing to execute an 8-for-1 stock split. The transaction follows a period of extreme volatility for the NAND flash specialist, whose stock has attracted meaningful attention amid surging demand for memory and storage solutions.

Although stock splits do not change a company's underlying valuation, they can still influence investor psychology and trading activity. By reducing the price of individual shares in terms of absolute dollars, Sandisk is making shares more accessible to investors who prefer purchasing whole shares rather than fractional shares.

Prepare for volatility in either direction this week

Ultimately, the combination of Nvidia's earnings, Anthropic's IPO, the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes, and Sandisk's stock split makes this an unusually eventful week for Wall Street. Investors should pay attention to any comments around Nvidia's leadership outlook, Anthropic's reception among institutional investors, and any changes in the Fed's assessment of inflation and interest rates. While these developments will likely fuel short-term volatility, their longer-term implications will depend on how they affect earnings and confidence in the broader economy.

news.Title: Microchip’s Earnings Rebound Meets a Softer Outlook
news.Content:
We just published our list of the 10 Highest Short Interest Large-Cap Tech Stocks Right Now , and Microchip Technology Incorporated ranked 8th on the list.

Technology stocks are facing a new test of investor conviction as hedge funds pull back from the artificial intelligence trade. Bloomberg reported on November 9 that hedge funds sold global technology stocks at one of the fastest weekly rates on record, citing Goldman Sachs prime brokerage data through November 6. Technology was the most heavily net-sold sector globally and in the US, with the percentage rate of selling roughly matching the benchmark set in Goldman's records dating back to 2016. The slump also resulted in the largest wave of single-stock net selling in four months.

The catalyst was not just another debate about overpriced stocks. According to Bloomberg, concerns about political opposition disrupting data-center buildout sparked an aggressive reconsideration of the AI trade. This raises questions about how quickly infrastructure projects can move forward and whether spending commitments would result in profitable growth. Insider Monkey's discussion of the fastest-growing AI stocks to buy highlights a related tension: strong demand and rapid revenue growth can coexist with pressure on share prices when investors question how the expansion will be financed.

The scale of that investment explains why the stakes are so high. According to Insider Monkey's analysis of the cheapest AI data center stocks to buy according to billionaires , the International Energy Agency estimates that hyperscalers would invest over $700 billion in new data centers in 2026. The same article cites CBRE research suggesting that supply in primary North American markets climbed 33.7% year-over-year to 10,903 megawatts in the first half of 2026, while vacancies declined to 1.4%.

The mechanics of short selling help explain what's at stake. A short sale generally involves selling securities that an investor doesn't own or has borrowed for delivery. The seller can profit by buying back the shares at a discount, but will lose money if the price rises. That said, heavily shorted stocks can react strongly when expectations improve. Short sellers may buy stocks to close off losing positions, potentially adding to an advance. The broader market's rebound shows how rapidly sentiment can shift: on November 9, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed 6.9%, its strongest session since July 30, as investors processed reports of near-record hedge-fund selling of technology stocks. Insider Monkey's coverage of AI stocks dominating the list of biggest winners subsequently reported that Nebius Group gained 15.44% on November 11, compared with the Nasdaq's 1.6% advance.

Story Continues

For investors considering bearish positions, the question is not whether AI demand will increase, but whether the companies that serve it can overcome infrastructure bottlenecks and turn that demand into profitable cash flow.

Microchip made the list on account of its market value of $33.57 billion and a short interest rate of 6.85%. Its 42.27% analyst upside indicates significant potential, while the short position presumably reflects concerns about whether the company's sharp earnings recovery can be sustained in a cyclical semiconductor market.

Microchip Technology Incorporated delivers semiconductors to a variety of areas, including industrial equipment and automotive applications. Its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results showed a significant turnaround, with revenue increasing 42.2% year-over-year and 9.2% sequentially to $1.622 billion, exceeding the midpoint of management's previous projection of $1.604 billion. GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders rose to $373.6 million, or $0.68 per diluted share, from $13.9 million, or $0.03 per share, the year before.

However, the December quarter outlook indicated a more measured near-term trend. Management expects revenue of $1.573 billion to $1.638 billion, a sequential decrease of 3% to 1%, and non-GAAP earnings of $0.87 to $0.95 per share. It also projected an adjusted gross margin of 64%-65% and an adjusted operating margin of 37%-38.5%, both lower than the September quarter's figures of 66.5% and 39.5%.

The company's balance sheet and valuation add another layer to the argument. The major concern is whether the earnings recovery can strengthen the balance sheet while still supporting shareholder payouts, a trade-off that Insider Monkey analyzed in its comparison of Microchip and competitor Lattice Semiconductor .

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MCHP as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Keeps On Going Down
news.Content:
For Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) investors, the bad news is a little less bad on Tuesday.

Ever since Nvidia's CEO resigned , the stock has been sliding. Shares of the GPU AI chips giant are now down about 25% for the month of November. (The good news is that as of 1:10 p.m. ET, Nvidia stock is down only about 1.5% more today.)

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

For Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) investors, the news is quite a bit worse. Not only is Sandisk stock down 32% in November. It's also down more than Nvidia stock today -- 2.7%.

Image source: Getty Images.

What's ailing Sandisk

Why are investors so down on Sandisk stock, whose own CEO -- unlike Nvidia's ex-CEO -- has not yet admitted to having an affair with an alleged Chinese Communist spy?

As I explained yesterday, Sandisk's problems basically stem from the fact that Nvidia AI chips and Sandisk's NAND flash memory chips are sold in pairs. You can't build an AI data center without both of them, and so if demand for Nvidia chips drops because of this scandal, Sandisk's sales might also suffer.

What's next for Sandisk

Granted, there's also the possibility that Sandisk might not take any hit at all. Nvidia's chip sales might not suffer after all, and even if they do, other producers of AI chips, such as AMD or Intel , might pick up the slack. In either of those situations, Sandisk's memory chips should still be in demand.

But here's the latest bad news: As my fellow Fool Travis Hoium reports, semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis thinks capital spending on AI chips in 2027 could be 19% below previous estimates, 2028 spending might be 28% below, and 2029 spending could fall 41 % below estimates.

How bad is this news? Well, luckily, it still works out to 24% annual sales growth in AI chips over the next five years. At a forward P/E ratio less than 4.0, and a PEG ratio less than 0.2 (!), I remain bullish on Sandisk stock.

news.Title: Sandisk's Earnings Face a New Risk in a Key Chip Market
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

GF Securities cut its 2027 price forecast for NAND flash aaazxswq2 memory, saying faster supply growth and weaker demand could leave the market oversupplied next year.

The firm sees Sandisk ( NASDAQ:SNDK ) as more exposed to falling NAND prices than Micron Technology ( NASDAQ:MU ) or SK hynix because its business is concentrated in flash storage.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Signs with SNDK.

Is SNDK fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

GF expects NAND prices to be flat in the first quarter of 2027 and fall in each of the next three quarters, Seeking Alpha reported. The firm pointed to softer demand for consumer electronics and weaker purchasing in China as production growth accelerates. NAND is the memory that stores data in devices such as smartphones and solid-state drives.

There are already signs of pressure in the spot market. TrendForce reported Tuesday that NAND spot prices fell about 20% in two weeks as Chinese traders reduced inventories. The drop shows what buyers are paying for immediate purchases. The next question is whether it carries over to the contract prices that suppliers negotiate with large customers.

GF expects Sandisk's earnings to be the most volatile of the three. The firm sees a stronger outlook for DRAM, the working memory used in computers and servers, and favors Micron, SK hynix and Samsung Electronics because they also sell DRAM and high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems.

Investors Takeaway

For Sandisk, the next test is whether lower contract prices start to squeeze margins, especially if customers cut orders at the same time.

For Micron and SK hynix, the question is how much stronger pricing for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory can offset weaker flash sales. The split matters because falling prices in one type of memory can hit suppliers' earnings very differently.

news.Title: KLAC is Overvalued at 9.37X P/S: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
KLA KLAC shares are overvalued, as suggested by the Value Score of F. In terms of the forward 12-month price/sales, KLAC is trading at 9.37X, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 4.96X. KLAC shares are trading at a premium compared with MKS MKSI, Entegris ENTG and Lam Research LRCX, shares of which are trading at 2.25X, 5.08X and 7.05X, respectively.

KLAC Stock's Valuation

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

So, is the KLA stock a buy, sell or hold at this level? Let's find out.

KLAC Jumps 28% in a Year: What's Driving the Stock?

KLA shares have returned 28% in the trailing 12 months, outperforming the broader sector. Despite its premium valuation, the company's strong position in semiconductor process control, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, rising demand for advanced packaging solutions and robust cash flow generation support its growth prospects.

The company is benefiting from increasing investments in AI infrastructure, which are driving demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing and process control solutions. The transition toward more complex chip architectures and leading-edge manufacturing nodes is increasing inspection and metrology requirements. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, semiconductor process control revenues increased 29% year over year to $3.75 billion, while wafer inspection revenues surged 37% to $2.11 billion.

KLAC expects the wafer fabrication equipment market, including advanced packaging, to reach the mid-$150 billion range in 2026 and exceed $200 billion in 2027. KLA's growing exposure to advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) represents a significant growth catalyst. Increasing adoption of heterogeneous integration and advanced packaging architectures is creating additional inspection and process control requirements. The company expects advanced packaging process control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in 2026, suggesting more than 70% year-over-year growth, nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced packaging market.

KLA's expanding installed base and increasing semiconductor manufacturing complexity are driving sustained demand for services. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, services revenues increased 14% year over year to $850 million, accounting for approximately 20% of total revenues. Strong demand reflects increasing equipment utilization, longer tool life cycles and customers' growing emphasis on productivity, yield optimization and system availability.

However, KLA continues to face supply chain constraints that could limit its ability to capitalize fully on accelerating semiconductor equipment demand. The company highlighted shortages of critical optical components and other long-lead-time materials, with average equipment lead times extending to approximately 12 months and certain advanced systems requiring even longer. KLA is also facing profitability challenges from persistently elevated memory costs, particularly DRAM used in its systems' image-processing capabilities. The company expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross margin of 62.5%, slightly below the 62.7% reported in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and its long-term target range of 63-64%.

The company's share price performance has suffered from these challenges. KLA shares have underperformed MKS, Lam Research and Entegris in a year's time. Shares of MKS, Lam Research and Entegris have returned 45.6%, 47.2% and 92.4%, respectively.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues is currently pegged at $4.73 billion, suggesting 43.4% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $1.42 per share, up 6% over the past 30 days. The figure suggests 59.6% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at $5.73 per share, up 5.3% over the past 30 days. The figure suggests 52.4% growth from the figure reported in fiscal 2026.

Conclusion: Is KLAC Stock a Buy?

Despite its premium valuation, KLA remains an attractive investment proposition, supported by its dominant position in semiconductor process control, accelerating AI infrastructure investments and growing demand for advanced packaging and HBM solutions. The company's expanding services business, robust cash flow generation and improving earnings estimates further strengthen its prospects. Although supply chain constraints and elevated component costs remain near-term challenges, KLA's growing backlog and favorable wafer fabrication equipment spending outlook provide strong revenue visibility. These factors suggest that KLAC's premium valuation is supported by its solid growth potential, making the stock an attractive buy for long-term investors willing to withstand near-term volatility.

news.Title: Is It Worth Investing in KLA (KLAC) Based on Wall Street's Bullish Views?
news.Content:
The recommendations of Wall Street analysts are often relied on by investors when deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock. Media reports about these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts changing their ratings often affect a stock's price. Do they really matter, though?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about KLA (KLAC) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

KLA currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.73, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 28 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.73 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 28 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 16 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 57.1% and 10.7% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for KLAC

Check price target & stock forecast for KLA here>>>

The ABR suggests buying KLA, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Is KLAC a Good Investment?

In terms of earnings estimate revisions for KLA, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 5.4% over the past month to $5.73.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for KLA. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for KLA may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: ASML vs. Lam Research: Which Chipmaking Stock is the Better Buy Now?
news.Content:
ASML Holding N.V. ASML and Lam Research Corporation LRCX are two premier technology firms benefiting from AI-driven chip demand and investments in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. Both players are well-positioned to benefit from growing demand for advanced computing, with ASML supplying the lithography equipment essential for manufacturing semiconductors and Lam Research supplying wafer fabrication equipment and related services.

ASML provides sophisticated hardware, software and systems that enable semiconductor manufacturers to produce increasingly smaller, faster and more energy-efficient chips. Its technologies are primarily used in the lithography stage of semiconductor manufacturing, in which complex circuit patterns are transferred onto silicon wafers.

Lam Research caters to the needs of semiconductor memory, foundry and integrated device manufacturers by providing them with integrated hardware, process, materials, software and process control. It serves the related markets that rely on semiconductor processes and require production-proven manufacturing capabilities, such as complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor image sensors and micro-electromechanical systems.

Let us try to analyze some of the competitive strengths and weaknesses of the companies to understand who is in a better position to maximize gains from the emerging market trends.

The Case for ASML

Rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is one of ASML's most powerful growth drivers. Training and inference workloads require increasingly powerful and energy-efficient processors, which are accelerating the transition toward smaller process nodes and more advanced memory technologies. The ongoing investments and continued progress in AI technologies are further boosting demand for both advanced Logic and Memory chips. Semiconductor manufacturers are accelerating capacity expansion plans, resulting in stronger commitments across ASML's product portfolio.

ASML's decision to materially increase manufacturing capacity further indicates stronger demand visibility. Based on strong customer commitments, the company expects to ship about 65 low-NA EUV systems in 2026, more than 50% above 2025, while DUV immersion shipments should be approximately in line with 2025. Management targets 30% additional capacity in 2027 and a significant increase in 2028 in tune with customer demand. Capacity expansion suggests customers are giving ASML greater visibility into their multi-year fab and technology plans.

However, management attributes the current demand environment primarily to AI-related investment and the resulting need for more advanced Logic and Memory capacity. Although this has produced unusually long order visibility for ASML, it makes the growth profile increasingly dependent on customers maintaining those expansion plans. A slower pace of customer investment would therefore affect both system demand and utilization of the larger production footprint ASML is preparing, resulting in elevated operational risks.

Story Continues

The Case for LRCX

Lam Research is extending its foundry and logic capabilities into advanced DRAM as customers adopt more demanding patterns and materials processes. The company has high exposure to memory, where AI is increasing storage and bandwidth requirements. Management expects 2026 wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending in the mid-$150 billion range and preliminary 2027 spending above $200 billion. DRAM is expected to lead percentage growth, followed by leading-edge foundry/logic and NAND. LRCX expects NAND demand across QLC, TLC and emerging SLC-class storage tiers to expand wafer capacity requirements. Its extensive NAND installed base supports opportunities from both technology upgrades and capacity additions.

AI workloads are increasing demand for HBM, chiplets and advanced packaging. Lam Research expects advanced packaging to remain a major growth driver as customers adopt more complex interconnects, through-silicon vias and bonding technologies. Its Syndion etch platform secured four new positions across multiple customers in advanced logic and HBM applications. Striker ALD also achieved multiple TSV liner wins, while VECTOR and TEOS 3D gained positions in bonding films and inter-die gap-fill applications. Lam Research has shipped panel plating systems to more than 20 customers across panel sizes ranging from 300-by-300 millimeters to 600-by-600 millimeters. Management expects its panel-level packaging market position eventually to exceed its established wafer-level packaging position.

However, semiconductor equipment demand remains cyclical and depends on customer capital budgets, end-market conditions and new fab construction. Although management expects WFE spending above $200 billion in 2027, limited cleanroom availability and component supply constraints could prevent equipment manufacturers from meeting demand fully. Trade restrictions and export controls remain a material risk because China contributed 35% of September-quarter 2026 revenues, increasing from 26% in June. The September increase reflected investment by both domestic and multinational customers, including mature-node foundry spending. However, management expects China's revenue contribution to decline substantially in the December quarter.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for ASML & LRCX?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ASML's 2026 sales implies year-over-year growth of 33.9%, while that for EPS indicates a surge of 66.4%. The EPS estimates have trended up 5.3% over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 sales indicates a year-over-year growth of 49.9%, while that for EPS suggests a rise of 65.2%. The EPS estimates have trended up 3% over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of ASML & LRCX

Over the past year, Lam Research has jumped 47.1% compared with the industry's growth of 10.8%. ASML has gained 40.1% over the same period.

Lam Research looks more attractive than ASML from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, ASML's shares currently trade at 8.81 forward sales, higher than 7.05 for Lam Research.

ASML or LRCX: Which is a Better Pick?

Lam Research currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), while ASML has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Both ASML and LRCX expect revenues and earnings to improve in the current fiscal. In terms of price performance, ASML has outperformed Lam Research, though it is trading at a slight premium. With a better Zacks Rank and solid fundamentals, ASML appears to be relatively better placed than Lam Research and is, therefore, a stronger investment option at the moment.

news.Title: 5檔ETF換股！00940「10進10出」 刪英業達、聯發科增南亞科
繼續拚AI！兆豐銀等10銀行 完成力積電300億元聯貸
news.Content:
面對全球人工智慧（AI）浪潮帶動半導體產業加速升級轉型，金融業亦透過資金支持與永續金融機制，協助企業強化競爭力並實現淨零轉型。由兆豐銀行統籌，與合作金庫銀行、華南銀行、彰化銀行及台灣土地銀行共同主辦之力晶積成電子製造股份有限公司300億元聯貸，今17日由力積電董事長暨執行長謝再居與兆豐銀行董事長董瑞斌完成簽約。

兆豐銀表示，共計10家金融機構踴躍參與，展現銀行團對力積電營運轉型及長期發展的支持。資金用途主要為償還金融機構借款，以及支應購置機器設備、興建、改建或購置廠房暨充實中期營運資金所需。此外，本案結合力積電持續推動節能減碳、減廢及資源循環之永續作為，將「節能率」、「廢棄物再利用率」及「製程用水回收率」三項ESG指標與授信條件連結，鼓勵力積電持續提升永續績效，實踐營運發展與環境永續並進。

隨著全球半導體產業朝人工智慧、高效能運算等應用快速發展，力積電近年積極調整營運及產品布局，持續深化記憶體、邏輯晶圓代工及3D AI Foundry等業務，並與國際記憶體大廠美光深化策略合作，推進HBM後段晶圓製造及記憶體製程技術合作，同時布局晶圓堆疊(WoW)、中介層(Interposer)及矽電容晶圓等AI應用領域，持續優化產品組合及營運體質。本次聯貸案將有助力積電整合中長期資金資源，支應後續營運轉型與技術發展所需，進一步強化長期競爭力。

兆豐銀行深耕聯貸市場多年，長期支持國內半導體、科技製造及重大產業發展，未來兆豐銀行將持續發揮金融核心職能，攜手優質企業掌握科技創新、產業升級及全球布局契機，共創穩健且永續之成長動能。
